children.translated_text: “Because of the threefold suffering”:
an introduction to this āryā verse is being made.

children.text: iha bhagavān brahmasutaḥ kapilo nāma tad yathā
children.translated_text: Here the venerable son of <s>Brahmā</s>, named <s>Kapila</s>, is as follows:
<s>Sanaka</s>, <s>Sanandana</s>, and third <s>Sanātana</s>,
<s>Āsuri</s>, <s>Kapila</s> himself, <s>Voḍhu</s>, and also <s>Pañcaśikha</s>:

children.text: ityete brahmaṇaḥ putrāḥ sapta proktā maharṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: these seven are declared to be the sons of <s>Brahmā</s>, the great seers.

children.text: kapilasya sahotpannāni dharmo jñānaṃ vairāgyam aiśvaryaṃ ceti
children.translated_text: Together with <s>Kapila</s> there arose <s>dharma</s> (virtue), knowledge, dispassion, and lordly power.

children.text: evaṃ sa utpannaḥ sann andhe tamasi majjajjagad ālokya saṃsārapāraṃparyeṇa satkāruṇyo jijñāsamānāya āsurisagotrāya brāhmaṇāyedaṃ pañcaviṃśatitattvānāṃ jñānam uktavān
children.translated_text: Thus, when he had arisen, seeing the world sinking in blind darkness through the succession of saṃsāra, and being full of true compassion, he taught this knowledge of the twenty-five tattvas to a Brahmin of the lineage of <s>Āsuri</s> who desired to know.
From knowledge of these, the destruction of suffering comes about.
One who knows the twenty-five tattvas may live in whatever āśrama he is;

children.text: jaṭī muṇḍī śikhī vāpi mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether wearing matted hair, shaven-headed, or wearing a topknot, he is liberated. There is no doubt about this.
This is what they say:
“Because of the assault of the threefold suffering, there is the desire to know.”

children.text: tatra duḥkhatrayam ādhyātmikam ādhibhautikam ādhidaivikaṃ ceti
children.translated_text: There the threefold suffering is internal, caused by beings, and caused by divine or cosmic forces.
Of these, the internal is twofold: bodily and mental.
The bodily is fever, diarrhea, and the like, produced by disorder of wind, bile, and phlegm.
The mental is separation from what is dear, union with what is not dear, and the like.

Suffering caused by beings arises from the fourfold group of living creatures: from humans, domestic animals, wild animals, birds, reptiles, gadflies, mosquitoes, lice, bedbugs, fish, crocodiles, sharks, and immobile beings, whether womb-born, egg-born, sweat-born, or sprout-born.

children.text: ādhidaivikaṃ devānām idaṃ daivaṃ divaḥ prabhavatīti vā daivam
children.translated_text: The divine is what belongs to the gods; or it is called daiva because it proceeds from the sky.
That which arises with reference to it consists of cold, heat, wind, rain, lightning-strikes, and the like.
Thus, just as inquiry is to be undertaken because of the assault of the threefold suffering,
where is it directed?
Toward the cause that strikes it down.

children.text: tasya duḥkhatrayasya abhighātako yo hetus tatreti
children.translated_text: That is, toward the cause which strikes down that threefold suffering.
If, with regard to the seen means, that inquiry is purposeless,

children.text: dṛṣṭe hetau duḥkhatrayābhighātake sā jijñāsāpārthā ced yadi
children.translated_text: if the inquiry is purposeless because there is a seen cause that strikes down the threefold suffering,

then for the twofold internal suffering there is indeed a visible remedy, through the procedure of the science of Āyurveda, through union with what is dear, avoidance of what is not dear, and decoctions of pungent, bitter, astringent substances and the like.
For suffering caused by beings, its removal is seen through protection and the like.
If you think, therefore, that because a visible remedy exists the inquiry is purposeless,
no.
Because there is no absolute and final removal.

children.text: yata ekāntato 'vaśyam atyantato nityaṃ dṛṣṭena hetunābhighāto na bhavati
children.translated_text: For by a visible means the removal does not occur absolutely, that is, necessarily, nor finally, that is, permanently.

children.text: tasmād anyatraikāntātyantābhighātake hetau jijñāsā vividiṣā kāryeti
children.translated_text: Therefore inquiry, the desire to know, is to be undertaken concerning another cause that removes suffering absolutely and finally.

children.text: yadi dṛṣṭād anyatra jijñāsā kāryā tato 'pi naiva
children.translated_text: If inquiry is to be made into something other than the visible, then even that is not so, one might say,
because the scriptural means removes the threefold suffering.
What is heard by tradition is anuśrava; what belongs to that is ānuśravika, scriptural.
And that is established from sacred tradition.
For example:

children.text: apāma somam amṛtā abhūmāganma jyotir avidāma devān
children.translated_text: “We have drunk soma; we have become immortal. We have gone to the light; we have found the gods.

children.text: kiṃ nūnam asmān kṛṇavad arātiḥ kim u dhūrtir amṛta martyasya ||
children.translated_text: What can hostility now do to us? What, O immortal one, can the malice of a mortal do?”

children.text: kadācid indrādīnāṃ devānāṃ kalpa āsīt kathaṃ vayam amṛtā abhūmeti vicārya yasmād vayam apāma somaṃ pītavantaḥ somaṃ tasmād amṛtā abhūma amarā bhūtavanta ityarthaḥ
children.translated_text: At some time the gods such as <s>Indra</s> reflected: “How have we become immortal?” Since we drank soma, that is, since we have drunk soma, therefore we have become immortal, meaning that we have become deathless.
Moreover, “we have gone to the light.”
“We have gone to, we have obtained, the light,” that is, heaven.
“We have found the gods.”
They have known the divine ones.

children.text: evaṃ ca kiṃ nūnam asmān kṛṇavad arātiḥ
children.translated_text: And thus, “What can hostility now do to us?”

children.text: nūnaṃ niścitaṃ kim arātiḥ śatrur asmān kṛṇavat karteti
children.translated_text: What, surely and certainly, can hostility, an enemy, do to us?

children.text: kim u dhūrtir amṛta martyasya dhūrtir jarā hiṃsā vā kiṃ kariṣyatyamṛta martyasya
children.translated_text: “What can the malice of a mortal do to an immortal?” Malice, meaning old age or injury, what will it do to an immortal, to a mortal man?

children.text: anyacca vede śrūyata ātyantikaṃ phalaṃ paśuvadhena
children.translated_text: And elsewhere in the Veda an ultimate result is heard of through animal slaughter:

children.text: sarvāṃllokāñjayati mṛtyuṃ tarati pāpmānaṃ tarati brahmahatyāṃ tarati yo yo 'śvamedhena yajata iti
children.translated_text: “He wins all worlds, crosses beyond death, crosses beyond evil, crosses beyond the killing of a Brahmin, whoever sacrifices with the horse-sacrifice.”
If, then, with such an absolute and final result taught in the Veda, inquiry into something non-earthly is purposeless, not so.
It is answered:
“The scriptural is like the visible.”
What is equal to the visible is “like the visible.”
Why is that scriptural means like the visible?
Because it is accompanied by impurity, destruction, and excess.
It is accompanied by impurity because of the killing of animals.
And so it is said:
“Six hundred animals are appointed on the middle day
of the horse-sacrifice, according to the injunction, lacking three animals.”

children.text: yady api śrutismṛtivihito dharmas tathāpi miśrībhāvād aviśuddhiyukta iti
children.translated_text: Although it is a duty enjoined by śruti and smṛti, nevertheless, because of its mixed character, it is accompanied by impurity.
For example:
“Many thousands of <s>Indras</s> and of gods, age after age,
have passed away through time; for time is very hard to overcome.”
Thus, because even <s>Indra</s> and the others perish, it is accompanied by destruction.
Likewise it is accompanied by atiśaya, superiority or difference.
For, on seeing a special quality in another, one would have suffering.
Thus even the scriptural means is like the visible.
If it is asked, “What then is better?”
the answer is given:

children.text: tadviparītaḥ śreyān tābhyāṃ dṛṣṭānuśravikābhyām viparītaḥ śreyān praśasyatara ity aviśuddhikṣayātiśayayuktatvāt
children.translated_text: “The opposite of these is better”: what is opposite to both the visible and the scriptural is better, more praiseworthy, because it is not accompanied by impurity, destruction, and excess.
How is that so? He says:
“From discriminative knowledge of the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower.”

children.text: tatra vyaktaṃ mahadādi buddhir ahaṃkāraḥ pañca tanmātrāṇy ekadaśendriyāṇi pañca mahābhūtāni
children.translated_text: Here the manifest consists of the great principle and the rest: intellect, ego-maker, the five subtle elements, the eleven faculties, and the five great elements.
The unmanifest is <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter).
The knower is <s>puruṣa</s> (conscious person).
Thus these twenty-five tattvas are called the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower.
From knowledge of these comes the highest good.
And it has been said:
"One who knows the twenty-five principles," and so on.

children.text: atha vyaktāvyaktajñānāṃ ko viśeṣa ity ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Now, what is the distinction among the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower? This is stated.
Root-prakṛti is pradhāna, because it is the root basis of the seven that are both prakṛti and vikṛti.

children.text: mūlaṃ ca sā prakṛtiś ca mūlaprakṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: It is both root and prakṛti; therefore it is root-prakṛti.
It is not a modification.

children.text: anyasmān notpadyate tena prakṛtiḥ kasyacid vikāro na bhavati
children.translated_text: It does not arise from anything else; therefore, as prakṛti, it is not a transformation of anything.
The seven beginning with mahat are both prakṛti and vikṛti.
Mahat is buddhi.

children.text: buddhyādyāḥ sapta buddhir ahaṃkāraḥ pañca tanmātrāṇi
children.translated_text: The seven beginning with buddhi are buddhi, ahaṃkāra, and the five tanmātras.
These seven are both prakṛti and vikṛti.

children.text: tadyathā pradhānād buddhir utpadyate tena vikṛtiḥ pradhānasya vikāra iti saivāhaṃkāram utpādayatyataḥ prakṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: For example, buddhi arises from pradhāna; therefore it is a vikṛti, a transformation of pradhāna. That very same buddhi produces ahaṃkāra; therefore it is prakṛti.
Ahaṃkāra too arises from buddhi, and so it is a vikṛti.
And because it produces the five tanmātras, it is prakṛti.

children.text: tatra śabdatanmātram ahaṃkārād utpadyata iti vikṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: There the sound-tanmātra arises from ahaṃkāra, and so it is a vikṛti.
Because ether arises from it, it is prakṛti.

children.text: tathā sparśatanmātram ahaṃkārād utpadyata iti vikṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise the touch-tanmātra arises from ahaṃkāra, and so it is a vikṛti.
In the same way, because it produces air, it is prakṛti.
The smell-tanmātra arises from ahaṃkāra, and so it is a vikṛti.
In the same way, because it produces earth, it is prakṛti.
The form-tanmātra arises from ahaṃkāra, and so it is a vikṛti.
In the same way, because it produces fire, it is prakṛti.
The taste-tanmātra arises from ahaṃkāra, and so it is a vikṛti.
In the same way, because it produces water, it is prakṛti.

children.text: evaṃ mahadādyāḥ sapta prakṛtayo vikṛtayaś ca
children.translated_text: Thus the seven beginning with mahat are prakṛtis and also vikṛtis.
And the group of sixteen is a transformation.

children.text: pañca buddhīndriyāṇi pañca karmendriyāṇyekādaśaṃ manaḥ pañca mahābhūtānyeṣa ṣoḍaśako gaṇo vikṛtir eva
children.translated_text: The five cognitive faculties, the five active faculties, the mind as the eleventh, and the five great elements: this group of sixteen is only a vikṛti.
A transformation is a vikṛti.
Puruṣa is neither prakṛti nor vikṛti.

children.text: evam eṣām vyaktāvyaktajñānām trayāṇām padārthānāṃ kaiḥ kiyadbhiḥ pramāṇaiḥ kena kasya vā pramāṇena siddhir bhavati
children.translated_text: Thus, by which and by how many pramāṇas is the establishment of these three objects, the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower, obtained, and by which pramāṇa is each obtained?
Here in the world, an object to be known is established by a pramāṇa.
For example, rice is measured by prasthas and the like, sandalwood and so on by a balance.
Therefore pramāṇa must be explained.
Perception.

children.text: yathā śrotraṃ tvak cakṣur jihvā ghrāṇam iti pañca buddhīndriyāṇi
children.translated_text: For example, hearing, skin, sight, tongue, and smell are the five cognitive faculties.

children.text: śabdasparśarūparasagandhā eṣāṃ pañcānām pañcaiva viṣayā yathāsaṃkhyam
children.translated_text: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell are precisely the five objects of these five, respectively.

children.text: śabdaṃ śrotraṃ gṛhṇāti tvak sparśaṃ cakṣū rūpaṃ jihvā rasaṃ ghrāṇaṃ gandham iti
children.translated_text: Hearing grasps sound, skin touch, sight form, tongue taste, and smell odor.
This pramāṇa is called perception.

children.text: pratyakṣeṇānumānena vā yo 'rtho na gṛhyate sa āptavacanād grāhyaḥ
children.translated_text: An object that is not grasped by perception or inference is to be grasped from the statement of a trustworthy authority.

children.text: yathendro devarāja uttarāḥ kuravaḥ svarge 'psarasa ityādi
children.translated_text: For example, <s>Indra</s> is king of the gods, the northern <s>Kurus</s>, nymphs in heaven, and so on.
What is not graspable by perception or inference is then grasped from authoritative statement.
Moreover, it has been said:
Tradition is indeed the statement of a trustworthy authority; they know one to be trustworthy because his faults have been destroyed.
One whose faults have been destroyed would not utter a false statement, because there is no possible motive.
One who is intent on his own proper work and free from attachment and aversion,

children.text: pūjitas tadvidhair nityam āpto jñeyaḥ sa tādṛśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: always honored by those who know that matter: such a person is to be understood as trustworthy.
Among these pramāṇas all pramāṇas are established.
<s>Jaimini</s> accepts six pramāṇas.
Now, what are those pramāṇas?

children.text: arthāpattiḥ sambhavo 'bhāvaḥ pratibhaitihyam upamānam ceti ṣaṭ pramāṇāni
children.translated_text: Postulation, possibility, absence, intuitive apprehension, tradition, and comparison: these are the six pramāṇas.
Among these, postulation is twofold: seen and heard.
Among them, the seen form is as follows.

children.text: ekasmin pakṣa ātmabhāvo gṛhītaśced anyasminn apy ātmabhāvo gṛhyata eva
children.translated_text: If self-existence is apprehended in one side, then self-existence is apprehended in the other side as well.
The heard form is as follows.

children.text: divā devadatto na bhuṅkte 'tha ca pīno dṛśyate 'to 'vagamyate rātrau bhuṅkta iti
children.translated_text: <s>Devadatta</s> does not eat by day, yet is seen to be stout; therefore it is understood that he eats at night.
Possibility is as follows.

children.text: prastha ity ukte catvāraḥ kuḍavāḥ saṃbhāvyante
children.translated_text: When "a prastha" is mentioned, four kuḍavas are inferred as possible.
Absence is defined as prior absence, mutual absence, absolute absence, and total absence.
Prior absence is as follows.
<s>Devadatta</s> in childhood, youth, and so on.
Mutual absence:
the absence of a pot in a cloth.
Absolute absence:
like a donkey's horn, the son of a barren woman, or a sky-flower.
Total absence, that is, posterior non-existence, is like a burnt cloth.
For example, from the sight of dry grain the absence of rain is inferred.
Thus absence is manifold.
Intuitive apprehension is as follows.

children.text: dakṣiṇena ca vindhyasya sahyasya ca yad uttaram
children.translated_text: That which is south of the <s>Vindhya</s> and north of the <s>Sahya</s>,
on the earth extending to the sea, is a delightful region.

children.text: evam ukte tasmin pradeśe śobhanā guṇaḥ santīti pratibhotpadyate
children.translated_text: When this is said, an intuitive apprehension arises that there are fine qualities in that region.
This is called knowledge born of intuitive apprehension.
Tradition is as follows.

children.text: bravīti loko yathātra vaṭe yakṣiṇī pravasatītyeva evaitihyam
children.translated_text: People say, for instance, "A yakṣiṇī lives in this banyan tree"; just this is tradition.
Comparison is as follows.

children.text: gaur iva gavayaḥ samudra iva taḍāgaḥ
children.translated_text: "A gavaya is like a cow"; "a pond is like the ocean."

children.text: etāni ṣaṭ pramāṇāni triṣu dṛṣṭādiṣv antarbhūtāni
children.translated_text: These six pramāṇas are included within the three, perception and the others.
Among them, first, postulation is included within inference.
Possibility, absence, intuitive apprehension, tradition, and comparison are included within authoritative statement.

children.text: tasmāt triṣveva sarvapramāṇasiddhatvāt trividham pramāṇam iṣṭam tad āha
children.translated_text: Therefore, because all pramāṇas are established within just the three, the accepted pramāṇa is threefold. He states this:

children.text: tena trividhena pramāṇena pramāṇasiddhir bhavatīti vākyaśeṣaḥ
children.translated_text: The remainder of the sentence is: "By that threefold pramāṇa, the establishment of the pramāṇas occurs."
For the establishment of what is to be known is from pramāṇa.

children.text: prameyam pradhānam buddhir ahaṃkāraḥ pañca tanmātrāṇyekādaśendriyāṇi pañca mahābhūtāni puruṣa iti
children.translated_text: What is to be known is pradhāna, buddhi, ahaṃkāra, the five tanmātras, the eleven faculties, the five great elements, and puruṣa.
These twenty-five principles are called the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower.

children.text: tatra kiṃcit pratyakṣeṇa sādhyaṃ kiṃcid anumānena kiṃcid āgameneti trividhaṃ pramāṇam uktam
children.translated_text: Among them, some are to be established by perception, some by inference, and some by scripture; thus the threefold means of valid knowledge has been stated.
What is its definition? He states this:

children.text: prativiṣayeṣu śrotrādīnāṃ śabdādiviṣayeṣvadhyavasāyo dṛṣṭaṃ pratyakṣam ity arthaḥ
children.translated_text: With respect to their respective objects, the determination made by the ear and the other senses regarding sound and the other sense-objects is what is seen, that is, perception.
Inference is declared to be threefold:
pūrvavat, śeṣavat, and sāmānyatodṛṣṭa.
Pūrvavat is so called because something prior belongs to it; for example:
From the rising of clouds one establishes rain, because this has been seen before.
Śeṣavat is as follows:

children.text: samudrād ekam jalapalaṃ lavaṇam āsādya śeṣasyāpy asti lavaṇabhāva iti
children.translated_text: Having obtained one pala of water from the ocean and found it salty, one infers that the remainder too has the nature of saltiness.

children.text: sāmānyatodṛṣṭaṃ deśād deśāntaraṃ prāptaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ gatimaccandratārakaṃ caitravat
children.translated_text: Sāmānyatodṛṣṭa is when, having seen that the moon and stars have reached another place from one place, one infers that they are moving, as in the case of <s>Caitra</s>.

children.text: yathā caitranāmānam deśād deśāntaraṃ prāptam avalokya gatimān ayam iti tadvaccandratārakam iti
children.translated_text: Just as, seeing a man named <s>Caitra</s> having reached another place from one place, one says, 'This man is moving,' so too with the moon and stars.

children.text: tathā puṣpitāmradarśanād anyatra puṣpitā āmrā iti sāmānyatodṛṣṭena sādhayati
children.translated_text: Likewise, from seeing a mango tree in flower, one establishes by sāmānyatodṛṣṭa inference that elsewhere mango trees are in flower.
This is sāmānyatodṛṣṭa.
Moreover, it is preceded by the sign and by the possessor of the sign.

children.text: tad anumānaṃ liṅgapūrvakaṃ yatra liṅgena liṅgyanumīyate yathā daṇḍena yatiḥ
children.translated_text: That inference is preceded by a sign where the sign-possessor is inferred by means of the sign, as an ascetic by his staff.

children.text: liṅgipūrvakaṃ ca yatra liṅginā liṅgam anumīyate
children.translated_text: And it is preceded by the sign-possessor where the sign is inferred by means of the sign-possessor.

children.text: yathā dṛṣṭvā yatim asyedam tridaṇḍam iti
children.translated_text: For example, having seen an ascetic, one infers, 'This is his triple staff.'
Āptaśruti is trustworthy testimony and the statement of a trustworthy authority.
Trustworthy authorities are teachers such as <s>Brahmā</s> and others.
Śruti is the Veda.

children.text: āptāś ca śrutiś cāptaśrutistad uktam āptavacanam iti
children.translated_text: The trustworthy authorities and śruti together are āptaśruti; what is spoken by them is called āptavacana, trustworthy statement.

children.text: evaṃ trividhaṃ pramāṇam uktaṃ tatra kena pramāṇena kiṃ sādhyam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Thus the threefold means of valid knowledge has been stated. Now, by which means of valid knowledge is what to be established? This is said:

children.text: sāmānyatodṛṣṭād anumānād atīndriyāṇām indriyāṇyatītya vartamānānāṃ siddhiḥ
children.translated_text: From sāmānyatodṛṣṭa inference comes the establishment of supersensible things, those existing beyond the senses.

children.text: pradhānapuruṣāvatīndriyau sāmānyatodṛṣṭānumānena sādhyete yasmān mahadādi liṅgam triguṇam
children.translated_text: Pradhāna and puruṣa are supersensible, and they are established by sāmānyatodṛṣṭa inference, because mahat and the rest are a sign characterized by the three guṇas.

children.text: yasyedaṃ triguṇaṃ kāryaṃ tat pradhānam iti
children.translated_text: That of which this three-guṇa effect exists is pradhāna.
And because what is unconscious appears as if conscious, therefore there is another overseer, puruṣa.
The manifest is established by perception.

children.text: tasmād api cāsiddhaṃ parokṣam āptāgamāt siddham
children.translated_text: And what is not established even from that, being remote from sight, is established from trustworthy tradition.

children.text: yathendro devarāja uttarāḥ kuravaḥ svarge 'psarasa iti parokṣam āptavacanāt siddham
children.translated_text: For example, that <s>Indra</s> is king of the gods, that there are the northern <s>Kurus</s>, and that there are apsarases in heaven: such remote matters are established by trustworthy statement.
Here someone says:
Pradhāna or puruṣa is not perceived.
And whatever is not perceived in the world does not exist.
Therefore those two also do not exist.

children.text: yathā dvitīyaṃ śiras tṛtīyo bāhur iti
children.translated_text: For example, a second head or a third arm.

children.text: tad ucyate 'tra satām apyarthānām aṣṭadhopalabdhir na bhavati
children.translated_text: To this it is said: even of existing things, non-perception occurs in eight ways.
That is as follows:

children.text: iha satām apy arthānām atidūrād anupalabdhir dṛṣṭā
children.translated_text: Here, non-perception of existing things due to excessive distance is observed.
For example, of <s>Caitra</s>, <s>Maitra</s>, and <s>Viṣṇumitra</s> when they are in another country.
Due to nearness.
For example, the non-perception of collyrium in the eye.
Due to injury to the sense faculty.
For example, the non-perception of sound and form by the deaf and the blind.
Due to the mind's lack of steadiness.
For example, a distracted person does not take in even what has been properly said.
Due to subtlety.
For example, atoms of smoke, heat, water, and mist, though present in the sky, are not perceived.
Due to obstruction.
For example, an object hidden by a wall is not perceived.
Due to overpowering.
For example, planets, constellations, stars, and the like, overpowered by the sun's brilliance, are not perceived.
Due to being mixed with things of the same kind.

children.text: yathā mudgarāśau mudgaḥ kṣiptaḥ kuvalayāmalakamadhye kuvalayāmalake kṣipte kapotamadhye kapoto nopalabhyante samānadravyamadhyāhṛtatvāt
children.translated_text: For example, a mung bean thrown into a heap of mung beans, a jujube or āmalaka among jujubes or āmalakas, and a dove among doves are not perceived, because they have been placed among substances of the same kind.

children.text: evam aṣṭadhānupalabdhiḥ satām arthānām iha dṛṣṭā
children.translated_text: Thus, in this world, eightfold non-perception of existing things is observed.

children.text: evam cāsti kim abhyupagamyate pradhānapuruṣayor etayor vānupalabdhiḥ kena hetunā kena copalabdhis tad ucyate ||
children.translated_text: So if it is accepted that these two, pradhāna and puruṣa, exist, then for what reason is there non-perception of them, and by what is there perception of them? This is stated:
Because of subtlety, there is non-perception of it.
That is, of pradhāna.
Pradhāna is not perceived because of its subtlety.
Just as atoms of smoke, heat, water, and mist, though present in the sky, are not perceived.
How, then, is it perceived?
It is perceived from its effect.
Having seen an effect, one infers the cause.
There is pradhāna as the cause whose effect this is.

children.text: buddhir ahaṃkārapañcatanmātrāṇy ekādaśendriyāṇi pañca mahābhūtāny eva tat kāryam
children.translated_text: Intellect, ego, the five subtle elements, the eleven senses, and the five great elements: these are its effect.
And that effect is dissimilar to prakṛti.

children.text: prakṛtiḥ pradhānaṃ tasya virūpaṃ prakṛter asadṛśam
children.translated_text: Prakṛti is pradhāna; its virūpa means different from it, unlike prakṛti.
And it is similar in form.
That is, it has the same form as well.

children.text: yathā loke 'pi pitus tulya iva putro bhavatyatulyaś ca
children.translated_text: Just as in the world a son may be both like his father and unlike him.

children.text: yena hetunā tulyaṃ atulyaṃ tad upariṣṭād vakṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: For what reason it is alike and unlike, we shall explain later.

children.text: yad idaṃ mahadādi kāryaṃ tat kiṃ pradhāne sad utāhosvid asad ācāryavipratipatter ayaṃ saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: This effect beginning with mahat: does it exist in pradhāna, or is it nonexistent? Because teachers disagree, there is this doubt.
For in this Sāṃkhya system the effect exists, while for Buddhists and others the effect does not exist.

children.text: yadi sad asan na bhavatyathāsat san na bhavatīti vipratiṣedhaḥ
children.translated_text: If existent, it is not nonexistent; if nonexistent, it is not existent. Thus there is a contradiction.
On this he says:
Because of the non-production of what is nonexistent.
The existent is not nonexistent.
There is no production of the nonexistent; therefore the effect exists.
Here in the world there is no making of what is nonexistent.

children.text: tasmāt sataḥ karaṇād asti prāg utpatteḥ pradhāne vyaktam
children.translated_text: Therefore, because there is production from what exists, the manifest exists in pradhāna before its arising.
Therefore the effect exists beforehand.
What else?
Because of the taking up of a material cause.
Upādāna means the cause; because that is taken up.

children.text: iha loke yo yenārthī sa tadupādānagrahaṇaṃ karoti
children.translated_text: In this world, one who wants a certain object takes hold of the material cause for that object.
One who wants curds takes milk, not water.
Therefore the effect exists beforehand.
And for this further reason:
because everything is not possible from everything.
There is no production of every thing in every place.
For example, gold does not arise in silver and the like, nor in grass, dust, and sand.
Therefore, because everything is not possible from everything, the effect exists beforehand.
And for this further reason:
because what is capable produces what it is capable of producing.

children.text: iha kulālaḥ śakto mṛddaṇḍacakracīvararajjunīrādikaraṇopakaraṇaṃ vā śakyam eva ghaṭam mṛtpiṇḍād utpādayati
children.translated_text: Here a potter who is capable, with clay, stick, wheel, cloth, cord, water, and other implements as the means and accessories, produces from a lump of clay only a pot, which is what can be produced.
Therefore the effect exists beforehand.
And for this further reason, because of the state of being a cause, the effect exists beforehand.

children.text: kāraṇaṃ yallakṣaṇam tallakṣaṇam eva kāryam api
children.translated_text: Whatever has the defining character of the cause, the effect too has just that defining character.
For example, from barley come barley grains, and from rice come rice grains.

children.text: yadāsatkāryaṃ syāt tataḥ kodravebhyaḥ śālayaḥ syuḥ
children.translated_text: If the effect did not exist beforehand, then rice plants would arise from kodrava grains.
But they do not exist so; therefore the effect exists beforehand.

children.text: evam pañcabhir hetubhiḥ pradhāne mahadādi liṅgam asti
children.translated_text: Thus, by these five reasons, the mark beginning with <s>mahat</s> exists in <s>pradhāna</s>.
Therefore there is production from what exists, not from what does not exist.

children.text: prakṛtivirūpaṃ sarūpam ca yad uktaṃ tat katham ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: How is what was stated as both unlike and like <s>prakṛti</s> to be understood? This is now explained.
The manifest, the effect beginning with <s>mahat</s>, has a cause.
That which has a cause is 'caused.'

children.text: upādānaṃ hetuḥ kāraṇaṃ nimittam iti paryayāḥ
children.translated_text: Material cause, cause, and occasion are synonyms.

children.text: vyaktasya pradhānaṃ hetur asty ato hetumad vyaktaṃ bhūtaparyantam
children.translated_text: The manifest has <s>pradhāna</s> as its cause; therefore the manifest, down to the elements, is caused.
The principle of intellect is caused by <s>pradhāna</s>.
<s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-maker) has intellect as its cause.
The five subtle elements and the eleven faculties are caused by <s>ahaṃkāra</s>; space is caused by the subtle element of sound.
Air is caused by the subtle element of touch.
Fire is caused by the subtle element of form.
The waters are caused by the subtle element of taste.
Earth is caused by the subtle element of smell.
In this way the manifest, down to the elements, has a cause.
What else? It is impermanent.
Because it arises from something else.

children.text: yathā mṛtpiṇḍād utpadyate ghaṭaḥ sa cānityaḥ
children.translated_text: For example, a pot arises from a lump of clay, and it is impermanent.
What else? It is non-pervasive.
That means it is not all-pervading.
<s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> are all-pervading; the manifest is not so.
What else? It is active.
At the time of transmigration it transmigrates.

children.text: trayodaśavidhena karaṇena saṃyuktam sūkṣmaṃ śarīram āśritya saṃsarati
children.translated_text: Joined with the thirteenfold instrument, it transmigrates by taking support in the subtle body.
Therefore it is active.
What else? It is manifold.

children.text: buddhir ahaṃkāraḥ pañca tanmātrāṇy ekādaśendriyāṇi pañca mahābhūtāni ceti
children.translated_text: That is, intellect, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, the five subtle elements, the eleven faculties, and the five great elements.
What else? It is dependent.
It depends on its own cause.

children.text: pradhānāśritā buddhir buddhim āśrito 'haṃkāro 'haṃkārāśritānyekādaśendriyāṇi pañca tanmātrāṇi pañcatanmātrāśritāni pañca mahābhūtānīti
children.translated_text: Intellect depends on <s>pradhāna</s>; <s>ahaṃkāra</s> depends on intellect; the eleven faculties and the five subtle elements depend on <s>ahaṃkāra</s>; and the five great elements depend on the five subtle elements.
And what else? It is a mark.
It is connected with dissolution.

children.text: layakāle pañca mahābhūtāni tanmātreṣu līyante tāny ekādaśendriyaiḥ sahāhaṃkāre sa ca buddhau sā ca pradhāne layaṃ yātīti
children.translated_text: At the time of dissolution the five great elements dissolve into the subtle elements; those, together with the eleven faculties, dissolve into <s>ahaṃkāra</s>; that dissolves into intellect; and intellect goes to dissolution in <s>pradhāna</s>.
Likewise it has parts.
The parts are sound, touch, taste, form, and smell; it exists together with them.
What else? It depends on another.
It does not arise by its own power.

children.text: yathā pradhānatantrā buddhir buddhitantro 'haṃkāro 'haṃkāratantrāṇi tanmātrāṇīndriyāṇi ca tanmātratantrāṇi pañca mahābhūtāni ca
children.translated_text: For example, intellect is dependent on <s>pradhāna</s>; <s>ahaṃkāra</s> is dependent on intellect; the subtle elements and the faculties are dependent on <s>ahaṃkāra</s>; and the five great elements are dependent on the subtle elements.
Thus the manifest has been explained as dependent on another, subject to another.
Now we shall explain the unmanifest.
The unmanifest is the opposite.

children.text: etair eva guṇair yathoktair viparītam avyaktam
children.translated_text: The unmanifest is the opposite with respect to precisely these qualities as stated.
The manifest was said to have a cause.
For there is nothing beyond <s>pradhāna</s>.
Because <s>pradhāna</s> is not produced, the unmanifest is without a cause.
Likewise the manifest is impermanent.
The unmanifest is eternal because it is not produced.

children.text: na hi bhūtānīva kutaścid utpadyata iti nityaṃ pradhānam
children.translated_text: For <s>pradhāna</s> does not arise from anything, as the elements do; therefore <s>pradhāna</s> is eternal.

children.text: kim cāvyāpi vyaktam vyāpi pradhānaṃ sarvagatatvāt
children.translated_text: And the manifest is non-pervasive; <s>pradhāna</s> is pervasive because it is all-pervading.

children.text: sakriyaṃ vyaktam akriyam avyaktam sarvagatatvād eva
children.translated_text: The manifest is active; the unmanifest is inactive, precisely because it is all-pervading.
Likewise the manifest is manifold; <s>pradhāna</s> is one because it is the cause.

children.text: trayāṇāṃ lokānāṃ pradhānam ekaṃ kāraṇaṃ tasmād ekaṃ pradhānam
children.translated_text: <s>Pradhāna</s> is the single cause of the three worlds; therefore <s>pradhāna</s> is one.
Likewise the manifest is dependent; the unmanifest is independent because it is not an effect.

children.text: na hi pradhānād asti kiṃcit paraṃ yasya pradhānaṃ kāryaṃ syāt
children.translated_text: For there is nothing beyond <s>pradhāna</s> of which <s>pradhāna</s> would be an effect.

children.text: tathā vyaktaṃ liṅgam aliṅgam avyaktaṃ nityatvāt
children.translated_text: Likewise the manifest is a mark; the unmanifest is without mark because it is eternal.

children.text: mahadādi liṅgam pralayakāle parasparaṃ pralīyate naivaṃ pradhānam
children.translated_text: The mark beginning with <s>mahat</s> dissolves mutually at the time of cosmic dissolution; <s>pradhāna</s> is not so.
Therefore <s>pradhāna</s> is without mark.
Likewise the manifest has parts; the unmanifest is partless.
For sound, touch, taste, form, and smell do not exist in <s>pradhāna</s>.

children.text: tathā paratantram vyaktam svatantram avyaktam prabhavaty ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise the manifest is dependent on another; the unmanifest is independent and arises by its own power.

children.text: evam vyaktāvyaktayor vaidharmyam uktaṃ sādharmyam ucyate
children.translated_text: Thus the dissimilarity of the manifest and the unmanifest has been stated; their similarity is now stated.
This is what was stated as 'also similar.'
The manifest consists of the three guṇas.
That in which the three guṇas, <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, exist is so called.
The manifest is non-discriminating.
That means it has no discrimination.

children.text: idaṃ vyaktam ime guṇā iti na vivekaṃ kartuṃ yātyayaṃ gaur ayam aśva iti yathā
children.translated_text: It cannot make the discrimination, 'This is the manifest, these are the guṇas,' just as one may say, 'This is a cow, this is a horse.'

children.text: ye guṇās tad vyaktaṃ yad vyaktaṃ te ca guṇā iti
children.translated_text: Whatever the guṇas are, that is the manifest; and whatever the manifest is, those are the guṇas.
Likewise the manifest is an object; this means something to be enjoyed.
Because it is the object of all <s>puruṣas</s>.
Likewise the manifest is common.
Because it is shared by all, like a slave woman bought for a price.
The manifest is unconscious.
The meaning is that it does not apprehend pleasure, pain, and delusion.
Likewise the manifest has the property of production.

children.text: tadyathā buddher ahaṃkāraḥ prasūyate tasmāt pañca tanmātrāṇyekādaśendriyāṇi ca prasūyante tanmātrebhyaḥ pañca mahābhūtānīti
children.translated_text: For example, ahaṃkāra is produced from buddhi; from that are produced the five tanmātras and the eleven faculties; and from the tanmātras the five great elements are produced.
Thus these properties of the manifest, ending with the property of production, have been stated.

children.text: evam ebhir avyaktaṃ sarūpaṃ yathā vyaktaṃ tathā pradhānam iti
children.translated_text: In this way, by these characteristics, the unmanifest is of the same form: just as the manifest is, so is pradhāna.

children.text: tatra triguṇaṃ vyaktam avyaktam api triguṇam
children.translated_text: There the manifest consists of the three guṇas; the unmanifest also consists of the three guṇas.
That of which this effect, beginning with mahat, consists of the three guṇas,

children.text: iha yadātmakaṃ kāraṇaṃ tadātmakaṃ kāryam iti
children.translated_text: for here an effect has the same nature as its cause.

children.text: yathā kṛṣṇatantukṛtaḥ kṛṣṇa eva paṭo bhavati
children.translated_text: For example, a cloth made from black threads is itself black.
Likewise the manifest is non-discriminating.
Pradhāna too is not distinguished from the guṇas.

children.text: anye guṇā anyat pradhānam evaṃ vivektuṃ na yāti
children.translated_text: One cannot discriminate, 'the guṇas are one thing, pradhāna another.'
That pradhāna is therefore non-discriminating.

children.text: tathā viṣayo vyaktaṃ pradhānam api sarvapuruṣaviṣayabhūtatvād viṣaya iti
children.translated_text: Likewise the manifest is an object; pradhāna too is called an object because it is the object for all puruṣas.

children.text: tathā sāmānyaṃ vyaktaṃ pradhānam api sarvasādhāraṇatvāt
children.translated_text: Likewise the manifest is common; pradhāna too is common because it belongs to all in common.

children.text: tathācetanaṃ vyaktaṃ pradhānam api sukhaduḥkhamohān na cetayatīti katham anumīyate
children.translated_text: Likewise the manifest is unconscious; pradhāna too does not apprehend pleasure, pain, and delusion. How is this inferred?

children.text: iha hyacetanān mṛtpiṇḍād acetano ghaṭa utpadyate
children.translated_text: For here, from an unconscious lump of clay, an unconscious pot is produced.
In this way pradhāna too has been explained.

children.text: idānīṃ tadviparītas tathā ca pumān ityetad vyākhyāyate
children.translated_text: Now the statement 'and puruṣa is likewise the opposite of these' is explained.
'The opposite of these' means that puruṣa is the opposite of those two, the manifest and the unmanifest.
That is as follows.
The manifest and the unmanifest have the three guṇas; puruṣa is without guṇas.

children.text: aviveki vyaktam avyaktaṃ ca vivekī puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: The manifest and the unmanifest are non-discriminating; puruṣa is discriminating.

children.text: tathā viṣayo vyaktam avyaktaṃ cāviṣayaḥ puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise the manifest and the unmanifest are objects; puruṣa is not an object.

children.text: tathā sāmānyaṃ vyaktam avyaktaṃ cāsāmānyaḥ puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise the manifest and the unmanifest are common; puruṣa is not common.

children.text: acetanaṃ vyaktam avyaktaṃ ca cetanaḥ puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: The manifest and the unmanifest are unconscious; puruṣa is conscious.
It apprehends and knows pleasure, pain, and delusion.
The manifest and pradhāna have the property of production; puruṣa does not have the property of production.
For nothing at all is produced from puruṣa.
Therefore it was said, 'puruṣa is the opposite of these.'

children.text: tad uktaṃ tathā ca pumān iti
children.translated_text: That is what was stated by 'and puruṣa is likewise.'

children.text: tat pūrvasyām āryāyāṃ pradhānam ahetumad yathā vyākhyātaṃ tathā ca pumān
children.translated_text: Just as pradhāna was explained in the preceding āryā verse as without a cause, so too is puruṣa.

children.text: tad yathā hetumad anityam ityādi vyaktaṃ tadviparītam avyaktam
children.translated_text: That is, the manifest is caused, impermanent, and so on; the unmanifest is the opposite of that.

children.text: tatra hetumad vyaktam ahetumat pradhānaṃ tathā ca pumān ahetumān anutpādyatvāt
children.translated_text: There the manifest has a cause; pradhāna is without a cause. So too puruṣa is without a cause, because it is not something produced.
The manifest is impermanent; pradhāna is permanent.
Likewise puruṣa is permanent.
The manifest is non-pervasive; pradhāna is pervasive.
And likewise puruṣa is pervasive, because it is present everywhere.

children.text: sakriyaṃ vyaktam akriyaṃ pradhānaṃ tathā ca pumān akriyaḥ sarvagatatvād eva
children.translated_text: The manifest is active; pradhāna is inactive. Likewise puruṣa is inactive, precisely because it is present everywhere.

children.text: anekaṃ vyaktam ekam avyaktaṃ tathā pumān apy ekaḥ
children.translated_text: The manifest is many; the unmanifest is one. Likewise puruṣa too is one.

children.text: āśritaṃ vyaktam anāśritam avyaktaṃ tathā ca pumān anāśritaḥ
children.translated_text: The manifest is dependent; the unmanifest is independent. Likewise puruṣa is independent.

children.text: liṅgaṃ vyaktam aliṅgam avyaktaṃ tathā ca pumān apyaliṅgaḥ
children.translated_text: The manifest is a mark; the unmanifest is without a mark. Likewise puruṣa too is without a mark.
That is, it does not dissolve anywhere.
The manifest has parts; the unmanifest is without parts.
Likewise puruṣa is without parts.
For in puruṣa there are no parts such as sound and the rest.

children.text: kiṃ ca paratantraṃ vyaktaṃ svatantram avyaktam
children.translated_text: Moreover, the manifest is dependent on another; the unmanifest is independent.

children.text: tathā ca pumān api svatantra ātmanaḥ prabhavatīty arthaḥ
children.translated_text: And likewise puruṣa too is independent; the meaning is that it is master of itself.

children.text: evam etad avyaktapuruṣayoḥ sādharmyaṃ vyākhyātaṃ pūrvasyām āryāyām
children.translated_text: Thus this similarity between the unmanifest and puruṣa has been explained in the preceding āryā verse.

children.text: vyaktapradhānayoḥ sādharmyaṃ puruṣasya vaidharmyaṃ ca triguṇam avivekītyādi prakṛtyāryāyāṃ vyākhyātam
children.translated_text: The similarity between the manifest and pradhāna, and the dissimilarity of puruṣa, were explained in the āryā verse beginning 'consisting of the three guṇas, non-discriminating,' and so on.

children.text: tatra yad uktaṃ triguṇam iti vyaktam avyaktaṃ ca
children.translated_text: There, what was stated as 'consisting of the three guṇas' refers to both the manifest and the unmanifest.
Then what are those guṇas?
In order to set forth their own nature, he says this:
The guṇas are of the nature of pleasure, of the nature of displeasure, and of the nature of despondency; the meaning is sattva, rajas, and tamas.
Among these, sattva is of the nature of pleasure.
Pleasure is happiness; it has that as its nature.
Rajas is of the nature of displeasure.
Displeasure is pain.
Tamas is of the nature of despondency.
Despondency is delusion.
Likewise they have illumination, activity, and restraint as their purposes.

children.text: arthaśabdaḥ sāmarthyavācī prakāśārthaṃ sattvaṃ prakāśasamartham ity arthaḥ
children.translated_text: The word 'purpose' denotes capacity: sattva is for illumination, meaning that it is capable of illumination.
Rajas is for activity.
Tamas is for restraint.
The meaning is that it is capable of stability.
Thus the guṇas have the character of illumination, action, and stability.
Likewise they have the functions of mutual overpowering, mutual dependence, mutual production, mutual pairing, and mutual operation.

children.text: anyonyābhibhavā anyonyāśrayā anyonyajananā anyonyamithunā anyonyavṛttayaśca te tathoktāḥ
children.translated_text: They are mutually overpowering, mutually dependent, mutually productive, mutually paired, and mutually operative; they are described in that way.
'Mutually overpowering' means that they overpower one another reciprocally.
They become manifest through qualities such as pleasure and displeasure.

children.text: yathā yadā sattvam utkaṭaṃ bhavati tadā rajastamasī abhibhūya svaguṇaiḥ prītiprakāśātmanāvatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: For example, when sattva becomes predominant, then, overpowering rajas and tamas, it remains with its own qualities, having the nature of pleasure and illumination.
When rajas predominates, it overpowers sattva and tamas by the property of displeasure and activity.
When tamas predominates, it overpowers sattva and rajas by its nature of despondency and stability.
Likewise the guṇas are mutually dependent, like dyads.
They are mutually productive, as a lump of clay produces a pot.
Likewise they are mutually paired; just as woman and man are a mutual pair, so are the guṇas.
And it has been said:

children.text: rajaso mithunaṃ sattvaṃ sattvasya mithunaṃ rajaḥ
children.translated_text: Sattva is the mate of rajas, and rajas is the mate of sattva.
The pairing of both <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s> is called <s>tamas</s>.
The meaning is that they assist one another.
And they have functions dependent on one another; they operate mutually.
For it is said, 'The guṇas operate among the guṇas.'

children.text: yathā surūpā suśīlā strī sarvasukhahetuḥ sapatnīnāṃ saiva duḥkhahetuḥ saiva rāgiṇāṃ mohaṃ janayatyevaṃ sattvaṃ rajastamasor vṛttihetuḥ
children.translated_text: Just as a woman who is beautiful and well behaved is the cause of every pleasure, while she herself is a cause of pain for co-wives and she herself produces delusion in passionate men, so <s>sattva</s> is the cause of the operation of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>.

children.text: yathā rājā sadodyuktaḥ prajāpālane duṣṭanigrahe śiṣṭānāṃ sukham utpādayati duṣṭānāṃ duḥkhaṃ mohaṃ caivaṃ rajaḥ sattvatamasor vṛttiṃ janayati
children.translated_text: Just as a king, always exerting himself in protecting his subjects and restraining the wicked, produces happiness for the good and pain and delusion for the wicked, so <s>rajas</s> produces the operation of <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s>.

children.text: tathā tamaḥ svarūpeṇāvaraṇātmakena sattvarajasor vṛttiṃ janayati
children.translated_text: Likewise <s>tamas</s>, by its own nature, which consists in covering, produces the operation of <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s>.

children.text: yathā meghāḥ kham āvṛtya jagataḥ sukham utpādayanti te vṛṣṭyā karṣakāṇāṃ karṣaṇodyogaṃ janayanti virahiṇāṃ moham
children.translated_text: Just as clouds, covering the sky, produce comfort for the world, by rain they produce activity in ploughing for farmers, and delusion in those separated from their lovers.
Thus the guṇas have operations dependent on one another.
And what else?
<s>Sattva</s> is light and illuminating.

children.text: yadā sattvam utkaṭaṃ bhavati tadā laghūnyaṅgāni buddhiprakāśaśca prasannatendriyāṇāṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: When <s>sattva</s> is predominant, then the limbs become light, there is illumination of the intellect, and the senses are clear.
<s>Rajas</s> is supporting and mobile.
It supports, therefore it is 'supporting'; it is an illuminator.

children.text: yathā vṛṣo vṛṣadarśana utkaṭam upaṣṭambhakaṃ karotyevaṃ rajovṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: Just as a bull, on seeing another bull, makes a strong support, so is the operation of <s>rajas</s>.

children.text: tathā rajaśca calaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ rajovṛttiścalacitto bhavati
children.translated_text: And likewise <s>rajas</s> is seen to be mobile; one whose mental state is affected by <s>rajas</s> becomes restless in mind.
<s>Tamas</s> alone is heavy and enveloping.

children.text: yadā tama utkaṭaṃ bhavati tadā gurūṇyaṅgāny avṛtānīndriyāṇi bhavanti svārthāsamarthāni
children.translated_text: When <s>tamas</s> is predominant, then the limbs become heavy and the senses become covered, unable to perform their own objects.
Here someone says:

children.text: yadi guṇāḥ parasparaṃ viruddhāḥ svamatenaiva kam arthaṃ niṣpādayanti tarhi katham
children.translated_text: If the guṇas are mutually opposed and accomplish an object only according to their own doctrine, then how is this possible?
Their operation with respect to an object is like a lamp.
Like a lamp means equal to a lamp.
Operation, as an instrument with respect to an object, is accepted.

children.text: yathā pradīpaḥ parasparaviruddhatailāgnivartisaṃyogād arthaprakāśaṃ janayatyevaṃ sattvarajastamāṃsi parasparaviruddhānyarthaṃ niṣpādayanti
children.translated_text: Just as a lamp, from the conjunction of mutually opposed oil, fire, and wick, produces the illumination of an object, so <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, though mutually opposed, accomplish an object.
An intervening question arises.

children.text: triguṇam aviveki viṣaya ityādi pradhānaṃ vyaktaṃ ca vyākhyātam
children.translated_text: The statement beginning 'the object is constituted by the three guṇas and is non-discriminating' has been explained with reference to both <s>pradhāna</s> and the manifest.

children.text: tatra pradhānaṃ upalabhyamānaṃ mahadādi ca triguṇam avivekyādīti ca katham avagamyate
children.translated_text: But how is it understood that <s>pradhāna</s>, which is being inferred, and the series beginning with <s>mahat</s> are constituted by the three guṇas and are non-discriminating and so on?
To this he says:

children.text: yo 'yam avivekyādirguṇaḥ sa traiguṇyān mahadādāvavyakte nāyaṃ sidhyati
children.translated_text: This quality beginning with non-discrimination, which exists because of the three-guṇa nature, is present in the series beginning with <s>mahat</s>; it is not established in the unmanifest.
On this it is said:
Because of the absence of its opposite.

children.text: tasya viparyayastadviparyayas tasyābhāvastadviparyayābhāvas tasmāt siddham avyaktam
children.translated_text: Its opposite is 'the opposite of that'; the absence of that is 'the absence of its opposite.' From that the unmanifest is established.
Just as where the threads are, there the cloth itself is.
The threads are not one thing and the cloth another.
Why? Because of the absence of its opposite.
In this way it is possessed of both the manifest and the unmanifest.
<s>Pradhāna</s> is remote; the manifest is near.

children.text: yo vyaktaṃ paśyati sa pradhānam api paśyati tadviparyayābhāvāt
children.translated_text: One who sees the manifest also sees <s>pradhāna</s>, because of the absence of its opposite.
For this further reason the unmanifest is established: because the effect has the nature of the aggregate of causes.

children.text: loke yadātmakaṃ kāraṇaṃ tadātmakaṃ kāryam api
children.translated_text: In the world, whatever nature the cause has, the effect too has that nature.

children.text: tathā kṛṣṇebhyas tantubhyaḥ kṛṣṇa eva paṭo bhavati
children.translated_text: Thus from black threads there is only a black cloth.

children.text: evaṃ mahadādiliṅgam aviveki viṣayaḥ sāmānyam acetanaṃ prasavadharmi
children.translated_text: In this way the inferential mark beginning with <s>mahat</s> is non-discriminating, objective, common, unconscious, and productive.

children.text: yadātmakaṃ liṅgaṃ tadātmakam ekam avyaktam api siddham
children.translated_text: Whatever nature the mark has, an unmanifest one of that same nature is also established.
Because of the three-guṇa nature, non-discrimination and the rest are established in the manifest.

children.text: tadviparyayābhāvād evaṃ kāraṇaguṇātmakatvāt kāryasyāvyaktam api siddham
children.translated_text: Because of the absence of its opposite, and thus because the effect has the nature of the qualities of the cause, the unmanifest too is established.
This objection is false.
It should not be said, 'Whatever is not perceived in the world does not exist,'

children.text: iti na vācyaṃ sato 'pi pāṣāṇagandhāder anupalambhāt
children.translated_text: because even existing things, such as the smell of stone and the like, are not apprehended.

children.text: evaṃ pradhānam apyasti kiṃ tu nopalabhyate ||
children.translated_text: In this way <s>pradhāna</s> also exists, but it is not perceived.
In the sentence 'the unmanifest cause exists,' there is a relation of action and participants.
Because of the limitation of the distinctions.

children.text: loke yatra kartāsti tasya parimāṇaṃ dṛṣṭam
children.translated_text: In the world, wherever there is a maker, a limit belonging to him is observed.

children.text: yathā kulālaḥ parimitair mṛtpiṇḍaiḥ parimitān eva ghaṭān karoti
children.translated_text: For example, a potter makes only a limited number of pots from limited lumps of clay.
So too with <s>mahat</s>.
The inferential mark beginning with <s>mahat</s>, limited according to its distinctions, is an effect of <s>pradhāna</s>.

children.text: ekā buddhir eko 'haṃkāraḥ pañca tanmātrāṇyekādaśendriyāṇi pañca mahābhūtāni
children.translated_text: There is one intellect, one ego, five subtle elements, eleven senses, and five great elements.

children.text: ityevaṃ bhedānāṃ parimāṇād asti pradhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ yad vyaktaṃ parimitam utpādayati
children.translated_text: Thus, because of the limitation of the distinctions, <s>pradhāna</s> exists as the cause that produces the limited manifest.

children.text: yadi pradhānaṃ na syāt tadā niṣparimāṇam idaṃ vyaktam api syāt
children.translated_text: If <s>pradhāna</s> did not exist, then this manifest too would be unlimited.

children.text: parimāṇācca bhedānām asti pradhānaṃ yasmād vyaktam utpannam
children.translated_text: And because of the limitation of the distinctions, there is <s>pradhāna</s>, from which the manifest has arisen.
Likewise, because of correspondence.

children.text: iha loke prasiddhir dṛṣṭā yathā vratadhāriṇaṃ baṭuṃ dṛṣṭvā samanvayati nūnam asya pitarau brāhmaṇāviti
children.translated_text: Here in the world a well-known inference is observed: on seeing a student observing a vow, one infers, 'Surely his parents are brahmins.'

children.text: evam idaṃ triguṇaṃ mahadādiliṅgaṃ dṛṣṭvā sādhayāmo 'sya yat kāraṇaṃ bhaviṣyatīti
children.translated_text: In the same way, seeing this inferential mark beginning with <s>mahat</s>, constituted by the three guṇas, we establish that there will be a cause of it.
Therefore, because of correspondence, <s>pradhāna</s> exists.
Likewise, because activity proceeds from capacity.

children.text: iha yo yasmin śaktaḥ sa tasminn evārthe pravartate
children.translated_text: Here, whoever is capable in regard to something proceeds only toward that object.

children.text: yathā kulālo ghaṭasya karaṇe samartho ghaṭam eva karoti na paṭaṃ rathaṃ vā
children.translated_text: For example, a potter, capable of making a pot, makes only a pot, not a cloth or a chariot.
Likewise <s>pradhāna</s> exists as the cause. Why? Because of the division of cause and effect.
That which makes is the cause; that which is made is the effect.
There is a division between cause and effect.

children.text: yathā ghaṭo dadhimadhūdakapayasāṃ dhāraṇe samartho na tathā mṛtpiṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as a pot is capable of holding curds, honey, water, and milk, but a lump of clay is not so capable,

children.text: mṛtpiṇḍo vā ghaṭaṃ niṣpādayati na caivaṃ ghaṭo mṛtpiṇḍam
children.translated_text: or as a lump of clay produces a pot, but the pot does not in this way produce the lump of clay,

children.text: evaṃ mahadādiliṅgaṃ dṛṣṭvānumīyate 'sti vibhaktaṃ tat kāraṇaṃ yasya vibhāga idaṃ vyaktam iti
children.translated_text: so, when one sees the mark beginning with mahat, one infers: there exists that distinct cause whose differentiation is this manifest world.
And further, because the manifold form is undivided.
The whole is the world.
Its form is manifestation.
The state of having the whole as its form is manifoldness.

children.text: tasyāvibhāgād asti pradhānaṃ yasmāt trailokyasya pañcānāṃ pṛthivyādīnāṃ mahābhūtānāṃ parasparaṃ vibhāgo nāsti mahābhūteṣvantarbhūtās trayo lokā iti
children.translated_text: Because that is undivided, pradhāna exists; for the three worlds, consisting of the five great elements beginning with earth, are not divided from one another, since the three worlds are included within the great elements.

children.text: pṛthivyāpas tejo vāyur ākāśam ityetāni pañca mahābhūtāni pralayakāle sṛṣṭikrameṇaivāvibhāgaṃ yānti tanmātreṣu pariṇāmeṣu tanmātrāṇyekādaśendriyāṇi cāhaṃkāre 'haṃkāro buddhau buddhiḥ pradhāne
children.translated_text: Earth, water, fire, wind, and ether: these five great elements at the time of dissolution, in the very order of creation, pass into an undivided state in the subtle elements, which are their transformations; the subtle elements and the eleven senses pass into ahaṃkāra, ahaṃkāra into buddhi, and buddhi into pradhāna.

children.text: evaṃ trayo lokāḥ pralayakāle prakṛtāv avibhāgaṃ gacchanti
children.translated_text: In this way the three worlds at the time of dissolution go into an undivided state in prakṛti.

children.text: tasmād avibhāgāt kṣīradadhivad vyaktāvyaktayor astyavyaktaṃ kāraṇam
children.translated_text: Therefore, from this non-division, as in the case of milk and curds, there exists an unmanifest cause of the manifest and the unmanifest.
And for this reason:

children.text: avyaktaṃ prakhyātaṃ kāraṇam asti yasmānmahadādi liṅgaṃ pravartate
children.translated_text: The unmanifest is established as an existent cause, because the mark beginning with mahat proceeds from it.
'From being three-guṇed' means from the three guṇas.
That in which the guṇas sattva, rajas, and tamas are present is three-guṇed.

children.text: tat kim uktaṃ bhavati sattvarajastamasāṃ sāmyāvasthā pradhānam
children.translated_text: What is said by this? Pradhāna is the state of equilibrium of sattva, rajas, and tamas.
Likewise, because of their aggregate.

children.text: yathā gaṅgāsrotāṃsi trīṇi rudramūrdhani patitānyekaṃ sroto janayantyevaṃ triguṇam avyaktam ekaṃ vyaktaṃ janayati
children.translated_text: Just as three streams of the Gaṅgā, having fallen on the head of <s>Rudra</s>, produce one stream, so the three-guṇed unmanifest produces one manifest world.

children.text: yathā vā tantavaḥ samuditāḥ paṭaṃ janayantyevam avyaktaṃ guṇasamudayān mahadādi janayatīti triguṇataḥ samudayācca vyaktaṃ jagat pravartate
children.translated_text: Or, just as threads gathered together produce a cloth, so the unmanifest, through the aggregate of the guṇas, produces mahat and the rest; therefore the manifest world proceeds from being three-guṇed and from aggregation.

children.text: yasmād ekasmāt pradhānād vyaktaṃ tasmād ekarūpeṇa bhavitavyam
children.translated_text: Since the manifest comes from one pradhāna, it must be of one form.
This is no fault: through transformation, like water, it varies because of the particular support of each respective guṇa.

children.text: ekasmāt pradhānāt trayo lokāḥ samutpannāstulyabhāvā na bhavanti
children.translated_text: The three worlds, though produced from one pradhāna, are not of equal condition.

children.text: devāḥ sukhena yuktā manuṣyā duḥkhena tiryañco mohena
children.translated_text: The gods are connected with happiness, human beings with pain, and animals with delusion.

children.text: ekasmāt pradhānāt pravṛttaṃ vyaktaṃ pratipratiguṇāśrayaviśeṣāt pariṇāmataḥ salilavad bhavati
children.translated_text: The manifest, proceeding from one pradhāna, comes about through transformation like water, because of the particular support of each respective guṇa.
The repetition in prati-prati expresses distribution.
The support of the guṇas is a guṇa-support.

children.text: tadviśeṣastaṃ guṇāśrayaviśeṣaṃ pratinidhāya pratipratiguṇāśrayaviśeṣaṃ pariṇāmāt pravartate vyaktam
children.translated_text: With reference to that distinction, namely the particularity of the guṇa-support, the manifest proceeds through transformation according to each respective particular support of a guṇa.

children.text: yathākāśād ekarasaṃ salilaṃ patitaṃ nānārūpāt saṃśleṣād bhidyate tattadrasāntaraiḥ
children.translated_text: Just as water of one taste, fallen from the sky, is differentiated by contact with various forms, by each different flavor,

children.text: evam ekasmāt pradhānāt pravṛttās trayo lokā naikasvabhāvā bhavanti
children.translated_text: so the three worlds, though proceeding from one pradhāna, do not have one single nature.

children.text: deveṣu sattvam utkaṭaṃ rajastamasī udāsīne tena te 'tyantasukhinaḥ
children.translated_text: Among the gods sattva is predominant, while rajas and tamas are indifferent; therefore they are exceedingly happy.

children.text: manuṣyeṣu raja utkaṭaṃ bhavati sattvatamasī udāsīne tena te 'tyantaduḥkhinaḥ
children.translated_text: Among human beings rajas is predominant, while sattva and tamas are indifferent; therefore they are exceedingly afflicted.

children.text: tiryakṣu tama utkaṭaṃ bhavati sattvarajasī udāsīne tena te 'tyantamūḍhāḥ
children.translated_text: Among animals tamas is predominant, while sattva and rajas are indifferent; therefore they are exceedingly deluded.
Thus, by the pair of āryā verses, the existence of pradhāna is accepted.
After this, in order to demonstrate the existence of puruṣa, he says:

children.text: yad uktaṃ vyaktāvyaktajñavijñānān mokṣaḥ prāpyata iti ||
children.translated_text: It was said that liberation is attained through knowledge of the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower.

children.text: tatra vyaktād anantaram avyaktaṃ pañcabhiḥ kāraṇair adhigatam ||
children.translated_text: There, immediately after the manifest, the unmanifest has been understood through five reasons.
Like the unmanifest, puruṣa too is subtle; now its inferred existence is explained: puruṣa exists.
Why?
Because an aggregate exists for the sake of another.
This aggregate beginning with mahat exists for the purpose of puruṣa.

children.text: ityanumīyate 'cetanatvāt paryaṅkavad yathā paryaṅkaḥ pratyekaṃ gātrotpalakapādapīṭhatūlīpracchādanapaṭopadhānasaṃghātaḥ parārtho na hi svārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is inferred because it is unconscious, like a bed. Just as a bed, as an aggregate of individual parts such as frame, feet, mattress, coverlet, cloth, and pillow, is for another and not for itself,

children.text: paryaṅkasya na hi kiṃcid api gātrotpalādyavayavānāṃ parasparaṃ kṛtyam asti ||
children.translated_text: for there is no function at all of the bed, nor of its parts such as frame and the rest, for one another.
Therefore it is understood:

children.text: asti puruṣo yaḥ paryaṅke śete yasyārthaṃ paryaṅkaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there exists a puruṣa who lies on the bed, for whose sake the bed exists.

children.text: tat parārtham idaṃ śarīraṃ pañcānāṃ mahābhūtānāṃ saṃghāto vartate ||
children.translated_text: So this body, an aggregate of the five great elements, exists for another.

children.text: asti puruṣo yasyedaṃ bhogyaṃ śarīraṃ bhogyamahadādisaṃghātarūpaṃ samutpannam iti ||
children.translated_text: There exists a puruṣa for whom this body, an object of experience, produced in the form of the experiencable aggregate beginning with mahat, exists.
And further, the self exists because it is the reverse of the three guṇas and so on.

children.text: yad uktaṃ pūrvasyām āryāyāṃ triguṇam aviveki viṣaya ityādi tasmād viparyayāt ||
children.translated_text: What was stated in the previous āryā verse as 'three-guṇed, non-discriminating, object,' and so forth: because of being the reverse of that.
It was said, 'And <s>pumān</s> is the opposite of that.'
Because of presiding over.

children.text: yatheha laṅghanaplavanadhāvanasamarthair aśvair yukto rathaḥ sārathinādhiṣṭhitaḥ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: Just as here a chariot, yoked with horses capable of leaping, plunging, and running, proceeds when presided over by a charioteer,
so too the body proceeds because it is presided over by the self.

children.text: tathā coktaṃ ṣaṣṭitantre puruṣādhiṣṭhitaṃ pradhānaṃ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: And so it is said in the Ṣaṣṭitantra: pradhāna, presided over by puruṣa, proceeds.
Therefore the self exists, because of being the enjoyer.

children.text: yathā madhurāmlalavaṇakaṭutiktakaṣāyaṣaḍrasopabṛṃhitasya saṃyuktasyānnasya sādhyata evaṃ mahadādiliṅgasya bhoktṛtvābhāvād asti sa ātmā yasyedaṃ bhogyaṃ śarīram iti ||
children.translated_text: Just as food compounded and combined with the six flavors, sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter, and astringent, is prepared for someone, so, because the mark beginning with mahat has no capacity for enjoyment, there exists that self for whom this body is an object of experience.
And further, because activity is for the sake of kaivalya.
The state of being alone is kaivalya.

children.text: tannimittaṃ yā ca pravṛttistasyāḥ svakaivalyārthaṃ pravṛtteḥ sakāśād anumīyate 'styātmeti yataḥ sarvo vidvān avidvāṃśca saṃsārakṣayam icchati ||
children.translated_text: And the activity which has that as its cause is inferred from activity undertaken for the sake of its own <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation): therefore, because every learned and unlearned person desires the cessation of saṃsāra, the self exists.

children.text: evam ebhir hetubhir astyātmā śarīrād vyatiriktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by these reasons, the self exists as distinct from the body.

children.text: atha sa kim ekaḥ sarvaśarīre 'dhiṣṭhātā maṇirasanātmakasūtravad āhosvid bahava ātmānaḥ pratiśarīram adhiṣṭhātāra ityatrocyate ||
children.translated_text: Now is it one self, presiding over all bodies like a cord consisting of a string of jewels, or are there many selves, presiding over each body? On this point it is said:

children.text: janma ca maraṇaṃ ca karaṇāni ca janmamaraṇakaraṇāni teṣāṃ pratiniyamāt pratyekaniyamād ityarthaḥ
children.translated_text: "Because of the fixed distribution of birth, death, and the faculties": birth and death and the faculties are "birth-death-faculties"; because of their fixed distribution, that is, because of their individual fixedness.

children.text: yadyeka evātmā syāt tata ekasya janmani sarva eva jāyerann ekasya maraṇe sarve 'pi mriyerann ekasya karaṇavaikalye bādhiryāndhatvamūkatvakuṇitvakhañjatvalakṣaṇe sarve 'pi badhirāndhakuṇikhañjāḥ syuḥ
children.translated_text: If there were only one self, then when one is born, all would be born; when one dies, all would die; and when one set of faculties is impaired, with the marks of deafness, blindness, muteness, crookedness, or lameness, all would become deaf, blind, crooked, and lame.

children.text: na caivaṃ bhavati tasmājjanmamaraṇakaraṇānāṃ pratiniyamāt puruṣabahutvaṃ siddham
children.translated_text: But this is not so. Therefore, because birth, death, and the faculties are individually fixed, the plurality of <s>puruṣas</s> is established.
And for this further reason: because activity is not simultaneous.

children.text: yugapad ekakālaṃ na yugapad ayugapat pravartanam
children.translated_text: "Simultaneous" means at one time; "not simultaneous" means not proceeding at the same time.
For activity with respect to <s>dharma</s> and the like is seen to be non-simultaneous.

children.text: eke dharme pravṛttā anye dharme vairāgye 'nye jñāne 'nye pravṛttāḥ
children.translated_text: Some are engaged in <s>dharma</s>; others are engaged in non-<s>dharma</s>, others in dispassion, and others in knowledge.

children.text: tasmād ayugapat pravṛtteśca bahava iti siddham
children.translated_text: Therefore, because activity is not simultaneous, it is established that there are many.
What else? And also because of the reversal of the three guṇas.
Because of the reversal in the condition of the three guṇas, the plurality of <s>puruṣas</s> is established.
For example, with birth being common, one person is sāttvika and happy;
another is rājasa and suffering;
another is tāmasa and deluded.
Thus, because of the reversal among the three guṇas, plurality is established.
It is now said that <s>puruṣa</s> is not an agent.
And because of that opposition.

children.text: tasmācca yathoktatraiguṇyaviparyāsād viparyayānnirguṇaḥ puruṣo vivekī bhoktetyādiguṇānāṃ puruṣasya yo viparyāsa uktastasmāt
children.translated_text: Because of that previously stated opposition among the three guṇas, because of the reversal: the reversal of qualities such as being without guṇas, discriminating, and an enjoyer, which was stated for <s>puruṣa</s>.
When sattva, rajas, and tamas are the agents, the witnessing status of <s>puruṣa</s> is established.
This is what is under discussion with regard to plurality.
The guṇas alone are the agents and proceed.

children.text: sākṣī nāpi pravartate nāpi nivartata eva
children.translated_text: The witness neither proceeds nor indeed ceases.
What else? Isolation.
The state of being alone is <s>kaivalya</s>; the meaning is otherness.
It is alone, other than the three guṇas.
Neutrality means the state of standing in the middle.
<s>Puruṣa</s> is neutral like a wandering ascetic.

children.text: yathā kaścit parivrājako grāmīṇeṣu karṣaṇārtheṣu pravṛtteṣu kevalo madhyasthaḥ puruṣo 'pyeṣu guṇeṣu vartamāneṣu na pravartate
children.translated_text: Just as some wandering ascetic, while villagers are engaged in ploughing and other tasks, remains alone and neutral, so too <s>puruṣa</s>, while these guṇas are operating, does not act.
Therefore it has the status of a seer and the condition of non-agency.

children.text: yasmānmadhyasthas tasmād draṣṭā tasmād akartā puruṣasteṣāṃ karmaṇām iti
children.translated_text: Because it is neutral, therefore it is a seer; therefore <s>puruṣa</s> is not the agent of their actions.

children.text: sattvarajastamāṃsi trayo guṇāḥ karmakartṛbhāvena pravartante na puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Sattva, rajas, and tamas, the three guṇas, proceed in the condition of agents of action, not <s>puruṣa</s>.
Thus the existence of <s>puruṣa</s> too has been established.

children.text: yasmād akartā puruṣastat katham adhyavasāyaṃ karoti
children.translated_text: Since <s>puruṣa</s> is not an agent, how then does it make a determination?
"I shall perform <s>dharma</s>; I shall not perform non-<s>dharma</s>."
Therefore it becomes an agent.
Yet <s>puruṣa</s> is not an agent.
Thus there would be a fault in both ways.
Therefore it is said:
Here <s>puruṣa</s> possesses consciousness.

children.text: tena cetanāvabhāsasaṃyuktaṃ mahadādiliṅgaṃ cetanāvad iva bhavati
children.translated_text: Through it, the mark beginning with <s>mahat</s>, joined with the reflection of consciousness, becomes as if conscious.

children.text: yathā loke ghaṭaḥ śītasaṃyuktaḥ śīta uṣṇasaṃyukta uṣṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as in ordinary life a pot joined with cold is cold, and joined with heat is hot,

children.text: evaṃ mahadādiliṅgaṃ tasya saṃyogāt puruṣasaṃyogāccetanāvad iva bhavati
children.translated_text: so the mark beginning with <s>mahat</s>, because of its conjunction with that, because of conjunction with <s>puruṣa</s>, becomes as if conscious.

children.text: tasmād guṇā adhyavasāyaṃ kurvanti na puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore the guṇas make determination, not <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: yadyapi loke puruṣaḥ kartā gantetyādi prayujyate tathāpyakartā puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Although in ordinary speech expressions such as "<s>puruṣa</s> is the agent" and "the goer" are used, nevertheless <s>puruṣa</s> is not an agent.
How so?
And when the guṇas are agents, the indifferent one becomes as if an agent in that way.

children.text: guṇānāṃ kartṛtve satyudāsīno 'pi puruṣaḥ karteva bhavati na kartā
children.translated_text: When the guṇas are the agents, even though <s>puruṣa</s> is indifferent, it becomes as if an agent; it is not an agent.

children.text: atra dṛṣṭānto bhavati yathācauraścauraiḥ saha gṛhītaścaura ityavagamyata evaṃ trayo guṇāḥ kartāras taiḥ saṃyuktaḥ puruṣo 'kartāpi kartā bhavati kartṛsaṃyogāt
children.translated_text: Here there is an example: just as a non-thief, seized together with thieves, is understood to be a thief, so the three guṇas are the agents; <s>puruṣa</s>, though not an agent, when joined with them, becomes an agent because of conjunction with agency.

children.text: evaṃ vyaktāvyaktajñānāṃ vibhāgo vikhyāto yadvibhāgān mokṣaprāptir iti
children.translated_text: Thus the division among the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower has been explained, from the division of which liberation is attained.
Now, what is the cause of the conjunction of these two, <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>?
It is said:
The conjunction of <s>puruṣa</s> with <s>pradhāna</s> is for the sake of seeing.
<s>Puruṣa</s> sees <s>prakṛti</s>, whose effects begin with <s>mahat</s> and extend down to the elements.
For this purpose there is also the conjunction of <s>pradhāna</s> with <s>puruṣa</s>: for the sake of <s>kaivalya</s>.

children.text: sa ca saṃyogaḥ paṅgvandhavad ubhayor api draṣṭavyaḥ
children.translated_text: And that conjunction of both is to be understood as like that of the lame man and the blind man.
For example, one is lame and one is blind.

children.text: etau dvāvapi gacchantau mahatā sāmarthyenāṭavyāṃ sārthasya stenakṛtād upaplavāt svabandhuparityaktau daivād itaścetaśca ceratuḥ
children.translated_text: As these two were traveling, after a great disaster in the forest caused by robbers against their caravan, they were abandoned by their own companions and, by fate, wandered here and there.
By their own movement they came into conjunction.

children.text: punastayoḥ svavacasor viśvastatvena saṃyogo gamanārthaṃ darśanārthaṃ ca bhavati
children.translated_text: Then, because each trusted the other's words, their conjunction came about for the sake of movement and for the sake of seeing.
The lame man was placed by the blind man on his own shoulder.
In this way the blind man goes by the road shown by the lame man mounted on his body, and the lame man is mounted on the blind man's shoulder.

children.text: evaṃ puruṣe darśanaśaktir asti paṅguvanna kriyā pradhāne kriyāśaktir astyandhavanna darśanaśaktiḥ
children.translated_text: Thus in <s>puruṣa</s> there is the power of seeing, but no power of action, like a lame man; in <s>pradhāna</s> there is the power of action, but no power of seeing, like a blind man.

children.text: yathā vānayoḥ paṅgvandhayoḥ kṛtārthayorvibhāgo bhaviṣyatīpsitasthānaprāptayor evaṃ pradhānam api puruṣasya mokṣaṃ kṛtvā nivartate
children.translated_text: And just as, when these two, the lame man and the blind man, have accomplished their purpose and reached the desired place, their separation will occur, so too <s>pradhāna</s>, after bringing about liberation for <s>puruṣa</s>, ceases to act.
<s>Puruṣa</s> too, having seen <s>pradhāna</s>, goes to isolation.
When the two have accomplished their purpose, their separation will occur.
What else? Creation is produced by that.

children.text: tena saṃyogena kṛtas tatkṛtaḥ sargaḥ sṛṣṭiḥ
children.translated_text: Creation, that is, emanation, is produced by that conjunction; therefore it is produced by that.

children.text: yathā strīpuruṣasaṃyogāt sutotpattis tathā pradhānapuruṣasaṃyogāt sargasyotpattiḥ
children.translated_text: Just as the birth of a son occurs from the conjunction of woman and man, so the origination of creation occurs from the conjunction of <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>.
Now, in order to show all the divisions, he says:

children.text: prakṛtiḥ pradhānaṃ brahmāvyaktaṃ bahudhātmakaṃ māyeti paryāyāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>pradhāna</s>, brahman, the unmanifest, the manifold self, and māyā are synonyms.
From <s>prakṛti</s>, which is without a mark, <s>mahat</s> arises.

children.text: mahān buddhir āsurī matiḥ khyātir jñānam iti prajñāparyāyair utpadyate
children.translated_text: <s>Mahat</s> arises under the synonyms buddhi, āsurī, mati, khyāti, and jñāna, all terms for cognition.
And from that <s>mahat</s>, ahaṃkāra arises.

children.text: ahaṃkāro bhūtādir vaikṛtas taijaso 'bhimāna iti paryāyāḥ
children.translated_text: Ahaṃkāra, bhūtādi, vaikṛta, taijasa, and abhimāna are synonyms.
From that comes the group of sixteen.

children.text: tasmād ahaṃkārāt ṣoḍaśakaḥ ṣoḍaśakasvarūpo gaṇa utpadyate
children.translated_text: From that ahaṃkāra arises the group of sixteen, whose nature is sixteenfold.

children.text: sa yathā pañca tanmātrāṇi śabdatanmātraṃ sparśatanmātraṃ rūpatanmātraṃ rasatanmātraṃ gandhatanmātram iti
children.translated_text: It is as follows: the five subtle elements, namely the subtle element of sound, the subtle element of touch, the subtle element of form, the subtle element of taste, and the subtle element of smell.
Then come the eleven faculties.

children.text: śrotraṃ tvak cakṣuṣī jihvā ghrāṇam iti pañca buddhīndriyāṇi
children.translated_text: The ear, skin, two eyes, tongue, and nose are the five faculties of knowledge.
Speech, hands, feet, anus, and generative organ are the five faculties of action.
The eleventh is mind, which has both natures.
This group of sixteen arises from ahaṃkāra.
Moreover, from the five come the five elements.

children.text: tasmāt ṣoḍaśakād gaṇāt pañcabhyas tanmātrebhyaḥ sakāśāt pañca vai mahābhūtānyutpadyante
children.translated_text: From that sixteenfold group, from the five subtle elements, the five great elements arise.

children.text: yad uktaṃ śabdatanmātrād ākāśaṃ sparśatanmātrād vāyū rūpatanmātrāt tejo rasatanmātrād āpo gandhatanmātrāt pṛthivī
children.translated_text: As has been said: from the subtle element of sound comes space; from the subtle element of touch, wind; from the subtle element of form, fire; from the subtle element of taste, waters; from the subtle element of smell, earth.

children.text: evaṃ pañcabhyaḥ paramāṇubhyaḥ pañca mahābhūtāny utpadyante
children.translated_text: Thus from the five atoms the five great elements arise.
As has been said:
Liberation comes from the discernment of the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower.
There, the twenty-threefold division from <s>mahat</s> down to the elements has been explained.

children.text: avyaktam api bhedānāṃ parimāṇād ityādinā vyākhyātam
children.translated_text: The unmanifest too has been explained by the verse beginning 'because of the measure of the divisions,' and so on.
<s>Puruṣa</s> too has been explained by reasons such as 'because the aggregate exists for another's sake,' and so on.
Thus these are the twenty-five tattvas.
Whoever knows that the three worlds are pervaded by them
knows their being, their existence, as tattva.
As has been said:
One who knows the twenty-five tattvas, wherever he may dwell in any āśrama,

children.text: jaṭī muṇḍī śikhī vāpi mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether wearing matted hair, shaven-headed, or having a topknot, is liberated; of this there is no doubt.

children.text: tāni yathā prakṛtiḥ puruṣo buddhir ahaṃkāraḥ pañca tanmātrāṇyekādaśendriyāṇi pañca mahābhūtānīti pañcaviṃśatitattvāni
children.translated_text: They are as follows: <s>prakṛti</s>, <s>puruṣa</s>, buddhi, ahaṃkāra, the five subtle elements, the eleven faculties, and the five great elements: these are the twenty-five tattvas.
There it was said that <s>mahat</s> arises from <s>prakṛti</s>.
What is its defining characteristic?
He states this:
Determination is the defining characteristic of buddhi.
The act of determining is determination.
As in a seed there is a sprout whose activity is future, so is determination.

children.text: ayaṃ ghaṭo 'yaṃ paṭa ityevaṃ sati yā sā buddhir iti lakṣyate
