children.translated_text: When one cognizes, 'This is a pot; this is a cloth,' the buddhi that exists in that way is what is characterized.
And that buddhi is eightfold, because of the distinction between its sāttvika and tāmasa forms.

children.text: tatra buddheḥ sāttvikaṃ rūpaṃ caturvidhaṃ bhavati dharmo jñānaṃ vairāgyam aiśvaryaṃ ceti
children.translated_text: There the sāttvika form of buddhi is fourfold: dharma, knowledge, dispassion, and lordship.
There, dharma means what is characterized by compassion, giving, restraints, and observances.
Among these, the restraints and observances are taught in <s>Pātañjala</s>.
Non-violence, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy, and non-possession are the restraints.
Purity, contentment, austerity, recitation, and devotion to the Lord are the observances.
Knowledge, illumination, comprehension, and shining forth are synonyms.
And that is twofold: external and internal.

children.text: tatra bāhyaṃ nāma vedāḥ śikṣākalpavyākaraṇaniruktachandojyotiṣākhyaṣaḍaṅgasahitāḥ purāṇāni nyāyamīmāṃsādharmaśāstrāṇi ceti
children.translated_text: There, the external consists of the Vedas together with the six limbs called phonetics, ritual, grammar, etymology, meter, and astronomy, and also the Purāṇas, logic, Mīmāṃsā, and Dharmaśāstra.
The internal is knowledge of <s>prakṛti</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: iyaṃ prakṛtiḥ sattvarajastamasāṃ sāmyāvasthāyaṃ puruṣaḥ siddho nirguṇo vyāpī cetana iti
children.translated_text: This <s>prakṛti</s> is the state of equilibrium of sattva, rajas, and tamas; this <s>puruṣa</s> is established, without guṇas, pervasive, and conscious.
By external knowledge there is esteem among people, meaning attachment from the world.
By internal knowledge there is liberation; that is the meaning.

children.text: vairāgyam api dvividhaṃ bāhyam ābhyantaraṃ ca
children.translated_text: Dispassion too is twofold, external and internal.
External dispassion is the absence of thirst for visible objects in one who is detached because he sees the faults of acquisition, protection, loss, attachment, and injury.

children.text: ābhyantaraṃ pradhānam apyatra svapnendrajālasadṛśam iti viraktasya mokṣepsoryad utpadyate
children.translated_text: Internal dispassion is what arises in one desiring liberation who is detached, thinking, 'Even <s>pradhāna</s> here is like a dream or a magical illusion.'
That is internal dispassion.
Lordship is the state of being a lord.

children.text: taccāṣṭaguṇam aṇimā mahimā garimā laghimā prāptiḥ prākāmyam īśitvaṃ vaśitvaṃ yatrakāmāvasāyitvaṃ ceti
children.translated_text: And that has eight qualities: minuteness, greatness, heaviness, lightness, attainment, fulfillment of will, lordship, mastery, and the power of realizing whatever one desires.

children.text: aṇor bhāvo 'ṇimā sūkṣmo bhūtvā jagati vicaratīti
children.translated_text: Minuteness is the state of being minute: becoming subtle, one moves about in the world.
Greatness is moving about after becoming great.

children.text: laghimā mṛṇālītūlāvayavād api laghutayā puṣpakesarāgreṣvapi tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: Lightness is such that, being lighter even than the parts of a lotus fiber or cotton, one can stand even on the tips of flower filaments.

children.text: prāptir abhimataṃ vastu yatra tatrāvasthitaṃ prāpnoti
children.translated_text: Attainment is that one obtains the desired object, wherever it may be situated.

children.text: prākāmyaṃ prakāmato yad evecchati tad eva vidadhāti
children.translated_text: Fulfillment of will is that, by mere wish, one accomplishes exactly whatever one desires.
Lordship is that by supremacy one rules even the three worlds.
Mastery is that everything comes under one's control.

children.text: yatrakāmāvasāyitvaṃ brahmādistambaparyantaṃ yatra kāmastatraivāsya svecchayā sthānāsanavihārān ācaratīti
children.translated_text: The power of realizing whatever one desires is that, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a pillar, wherever one's desire is, there by one's own will one carries out staying, sitting, and moving about.
These four are the sāttvika forms of buddhi.

children.text: yadā sattvena rajastamasī abhibhūte tadā pumān buddhiguṇān dharmādīn āpnoti
children.translated_text: When rajas and tamas are overcome by sattva, then a person obtains the qualities of buddhi beginning with dharma.
And what else? The tāmasa is the reverse of this.
The tāmasa form of buddhi is the opposite of this group beginning with dharma.
There, the opposite of dharma is adharma.
Likewise there are ignorance, non-dispassion, and lack of lordship.

children.text: evaṃ sāttvikaistāmasaiḥ svarūpair aṣṭāṅgā buddhistriguṇād avyaktād utpadyate
children.translated_text: Thus buddhi, with eight limbs through its sāttvika and tāmasa forms, arises from the three-guṇa unmanifest.
Thus the defining characteristic of buddhi has been stated; now the defining characteristic of ahaṃkāra is stated.
And the elevenfold group is the eleven faculties.
Likewise the group consisting of the subtle elements is fivefold, furnished with five characteristics.
It is furnished with the characteristics of the subtle element of sound, the subtle element of touch, the subtle element of form, the subtle element of taste, and the subtle element of smell.
From what characteristic does creation proceed? He states this.

children.text: sattvenābhibhūte yadā rajastamasī ahaṃkāre bhavatas tadā so 'haṃkāraḥ sāttvikaḥ
children.translated_text: When, in ahaṃkāra, rajas and tamas are overcome by sattva, then that ahaṃkāra is sāttvika.

children.text: tasya ca pūrvācāryaiḥ saṃjñā kṛtā vaikṛta iti
children.translated_text: And the former teachers gave it the name <s>vaikṛta</s>.

children.text: tasmād vaikṛtād ahaṃkārād ekādaśaka indriyagaṇa utpadyate
children.translated_text: From that <s>vaikṛta</s> ahaṃkāra the elevenfold group of faculties arises.
Therefore the faculties are sāttvika, pure, and capable with respect to their own objects.
Therefore it is called the sāttvika elevenfold group.
And what else? From <s>bhūtādi</s> comes the group of subtle elements; that is tāmasa.

children.text: tāmasābhibhūte sattvarajasī ahaṃkāre yadā bhavataḥ so 'haṃkāras tāmasa ucyate
children.translated_text: When, in ahaṃkāra, sattva and rajas are overcome by tamas, that ahaṃkāra is called tāmasa.
The name made for it by the former teachers is <s>bhūtādi</s>.

children.text: tasmād bhūtāder ahaṃkārāt tanmātraḥ pañcako gaṇa utpadyate
children.translated_text: From that <s>bhūtādi</s> ahaṃkāra the fivefold group of subtle elements arises.

children.text: bhūtānām ādibhūtas tamobahulas tenoktaḥ sa tāmasa iti
children.translated_text: Because it is the first source of the elements and is rich in tamas, it is said to be tāmasa.
Therefore from <s>bhūtādi</s> comes the group consisting of the five subtle elements.
And what else? From the taijasa comes both.

children.text: yadā rajasābhibhūte sattvatamasī bhavatas tadā tasmāt so 'haṃkārastaijasam iti saṃjñāṃ labhate
children.translated_text: When sattva and tamas are overcome by rajas, then that ahaṃkāra receives the name taijasa.

children.text: tasmāt taijasād ubhayam utpadyata ubhayam ityekādaśo gaṇastanmātraḥ pañcakaḥ
children.translated_text: From that taijasa both arise; by 'both' is meant the elevenfold group and the fivefold group of subtle elements.

children.text: yo 'yaṃ sāttviko 'haṃkāro vaikṛtiko vaikṛto bhūtvaikādaśendriyāṇyutpādayati sa taijasam ahaṃkāraṃ sahāyaṃ gṛhṇāti
children.translated_text: This sāttvika ahaṃkāra, the <s>vaikṛtika</s>, having become modified and producing the eleven faculties, takes the taijasa ahaṃkāra as its assistant.

children.text: sāttviko niṣkriyaḥ sa taijasayukta indriyotpattau samarthaḥ
children.translated_text: The sāttvika is inactive; joined with the taijasa, it is capable of producing the faculties.

children.text: tathā tāmaso 'haṃkāro bhūtādisaṃjñito niṣkriyatvāt taijasenāhaṃkāreṇa kriyāvatā yuktastanmātrāṇyutpādayati
children.translated_text: Likewise the tāmasa ahaṃkāra, called <s>bhūtādi</s>, because it is inactive, produces the subtle elements when joined with the active taijasa ahaṃkāra.
For that reason it was said, 'from the taijasa, both.'

children.text: evaṃ taijasenāhaṃkāreṇendriyāṇyekādaśa pañca tanmātrāṇi kṛtāni bhavanti
children.translated_text: Thus the eleven faculties and the five subtle elements have been made by the taijasa ahaṃkāra.
The sāttvika elevenfold group has been mentioned.

children.text: yo vaikṛtāt sāttvikād ahaṃkārād utpadyate tasya kā saṃjñetyāha ||
children.translated_text: What name belongs to that which arises from the <s>vaikṛta</s>, sāttvika ahaṃkāra? He states this.
The faculties beginning with the eye and ending with touch are called cognitive faculties.
It is called 'touch' because by it something is touched.
It is the faculty of the skin.

children.text: tadvācī siddhaḥ sparśanaśabdo 'sti tenedaṃ paṭhyate sparśanakānīti
children.translated_text: There exists a word 'sparśana' that denotes it; therefore this is read as 'the group ending in touch.'

children.text: śabdasparśarūparasagandhān pañca viṣayān budhyante 'vagacchantīti pañca buddhīndriyāṇi
children.translated_text: Because they cognize, that is, apprehend, the five objects: sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, they are the five cognitive faculties.
Speech, hands, feet, anus, and generative organ are said to be the faculties of action.
They are faculties of action because they perform actions.

children.text: tatra vāg vadati hastau nānāvyāpāraṃ kurutaḥ pādau gamanāgamanaṃ pāyur utsargaṃ karotyupastha ānandaṃ prajotpattyā
children.translated_text: Among them, speech speaks; the two hands perform various activities; the two feet do going and coming; the anus performs excretion; the generative organ gives pleasure through the production of offspring.
Thus the ten faculties have been explained by the distinction between cognitive faculties and faculties of action.

children.text: mana ekādaśaṃ kimātmakaṃ kiṃsvarūpaṃ ceti tad ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Mind is the eleventh; of what nature and of what form is it? This is now stated.
In this class of faculties, mind has both natures.
Among the cognitive faculties it is like a cognitive faculty, and among the faculties of action it is like a faculty of action.

children.text: kasmād buddhīndriyāṇāṃ pravṛttiṃ kalpayati karmendriyāṇāṃ ca
children.translated_text: Why? Because it constructs the activity of the cognitive faculties and also that of the faculties of action.
Therefore mind has both natures.
Because it forms intentions, it is an intender.

children.text: kiṃ cānyad indriyaṃ ca sādharmyāt samānadharmabhāvāt
children.translated_text: And what else? It is also a faculty because of similarity, because it possesses the same property.

children.text: sāttvikāhaṃkārād buddhīndriyāṇi karmendriyāṇi manasā sahotpadyamānāni manasaḥ sādharmyaṃ pratipādayanti
children.translated_text: The cognitive faculties, the faculties of action, and mind, arising together from sāttvika ahaṃkāra, establish mind's similarity to them.
Therefore, because of similarity, mind too is a faculty.
Thus these eleven faculties arise from the sāttvika, <s>vaikṛta</s> ahaṃkāra.
What, then, is the function of mind?
Intention is its function.
The functions of the cognitive faculties are sound and the other objects; those of the faculties of action are speech and the others.

children.text: athaitānīndriyāṇi bhinnāni bhinnārthagrāhakāṇi kim īśvareṇa svabhāvena kṛtāni yataḥ pradhānabuddhyahaṃkārā acetanāḥ puruṣo 'pyakartā
children.translated_text: Now, since these faculties are distinct and grasp distinct objects, were they made by God or by nature, given that <s>pradhāna</s>, buddhi, and ahaṃkāra are unconscious, and <s>puruṣa</s> too is not an agent?
On this he says:

children.text: iha sāṃkhyānāṃ svabhāvo nāma kaścit kāraṇam asti
children.translated_text: Here, for the Sāṃkhyas, there exists a certain cause called nature.
On this it is said:
Diversity and the external distinctions arise from particular transformations of the guṇas.
These are the eleven faculties: sound, touch, form, taste, and smell are the objects of the five; speaking, grasping, moving, excreting, and pleasure are the objects of the five.
And intention is the object of mind.

children.text: evam ete bhinnānām evendriyāṇām arthā guṇapariṇāmaviśeṣād guṇānāṃ pariṇāmo guṇapariṇāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus these objects belong precisely to distinct faculties, because of a particular transformation of the guṇas; the transformation of the guṇas is a guṇa-transformation.
Because of its particularity there is diversity among the faculties and also distinctions among external objects.

children.text: athaitannānātvaṃ neśvareṇa nāhaṃkāreṇa na buddhyā na pradhānena na puruṣeṇa svabhāvāt kṛtaguṇapariṇāmeneti
children.translated_text: Now this diversity is not made by <s>Īśvara</s>, not by <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, not by buddhi, not by <s>pradhāna</s>, and not by <s>puruṣa</s>; it is due to nature, through the accomplished transformation of the guṇas.
Because the guṇas are unconscious, they do not act.
They do indeed act.
How?
He will state it right here:
As milk, though unknowing, comes into activity for the growth of the calf,
so <s>pradhāna</s> comes into activity for the liberation of <s>puruṣa</s>.
Thus the unconscious guṇas act in the form of the eleven faculties.
The particular things too are made by them alone.

children.text: yenoccaiḥ pradeśe cakṣur avalokanāya sthitaṃ tathā ghrāṇaṃ tathā śrotraṃ tathā jihvā svadeśe svārthagrahaṇāya
children.translated_text: For this reason the eye is situated in an elevated place for seeing; likewise the nose, the ear, and the tongue are situated in their own places for grasping their own objects.

children.text: evaṃ karmendriyāṇyapi yathāyathaṃ svārthasamarthāni svadeśāvasthitāni svabhāvato guṇapariṇāmaviśeṣād eva na tadarthā api
children.translated_text: In the same way the faculties of action also, each according to its kind, are capable of its own object and situated in its own place by nature, solely because of a particular transformation of the guṇas; they are not for those objects in any other way.

children.text: yata uktaṃ śāstrantare guṇā guṇeṣu vartante
children.translated_text: For it is said in another śāstra: 'The guṇas operate among the guṇas.'

children.text: guṇānāṃ yā vṛttiḥ sā guṇaviṣayā eveti bāhyārthā vijñeyā guṇakṛtā evetyarthaḥ pradhānaṃ yasya kāraṇam iti
children.translated_text: The meaning is that the activity of the guṇas has the guṇas alone as its object; therefore external objects should be understood as produced by the guṇas alone, whose cause is <s>pradhāna</s>.
Now it is stated which activity belongs to which faculty.
The word 'only' has the sense of specification, in order to exclude what is not specific.

children.text: yathā bhikṣāmātraṃ labhyate nānyo viśeṣa iti
children.translated_text: For example, 'only alms are obtained,' and no other special thing.

children.text: tathā cakṣū rūpamātre na rasādiṣvevaṃ śeṣāṇyapi
children.translated_text: So the eye operates only with respect to form, not with respect to taste and the rest; the remaining faculties are the same.

children.text: tad yathā cakṣuṣo rūpaṃ jihvāyā raso ghrāṇasya gandhaḥ śrotrasya śabdas tvacaḥ sparśaḥ
children.translated_text: That is: form belongs to the eye, taste to the tongue, smell to the nose, sound to the ear, and touch to the skin.
Thus the activity of these faculties of knowledge has been stated.
The activity of the faculties of action is now stated.
Speech, grasping, moving about, evacuation, and pleasure are the activities of the five faculties of action; this is the meaning.

children.text: vāco vacanaṃ hastayorādānaṃ pādayor viharaṇaṃ pāyor bhuktasyāhārasya pariṇatamalotsarga upasthasyānandaḥ sutotpattiḥ
children.translated_text: Speech belongs to the voice, grasping to the hands, moving about to the feet, evacuation of the digested waste of eaten food to the anus, and pleasure, the production of offspring, to the generative organ.
The connection is: the object is the activity.
Now the activities of buddhi, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and mind are stated.
Their own defining characteristics are their own characteristic activities.

children.text: adhyavasāyo buddhiriti lakṣaṇam uktaṃ saiva buddhivṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: It was said that determination is buddhi's defining characteristic; that very thing is the activity of buddhi.
Likewise, 'self-conceit is <s>ahaṃkāra</s>'; and self-conceit is its defining characteristic and also its activity.

children.text: saṃkalpakaṃ mana iti lakṣaṇam uktaṃ tena saṃkalpa eva manaso vṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: It was said that mind is what forms intentions; therefore intention itself is the activity of mind.
For the three, buddhi, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and mind, the activity is their own defining characteristic.

children.text: asāmānyā yā prāgabhihitā buddhīndriyāṇāṃ ca vṛttiḥ sāpyasāmānyaiveti
children.translated_text: And the activity of the faculties of knowledge, previously described as uncommon, is also uncommon.
Now the common activity is explained.
The common activity of the instruments means the activity of the instruments in common.

children.text: prāṇādyā vāyavaḥ pañca prāṇāpānasamānodānavyānā iti pañca vāyavaḥ sarvendriyāṇāṃ sāmānyā vṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: The five winds beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>, namely <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, <s>samāna</s>, <s>udāna</s>, and <s>vyāna</s>, are the common activity of all the faculties.

children.text: yataḥ prāṇo nāma vāyurmukhanāsikāntargocaras tasya yat spandanaṃ karma tat trayodaśavidhasyāpi sāmānyā vṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: For the wind called <s>prāṇa</s> has its sphere within the mouth and nose; the pulsation that is its action is the common activity even of the thirteenfold instrument.

children.text: sati prāṇe yasmāt karaṇānām ātmalābha iti prāṇo 'pi pañjaraśakunivat sarvasya calanaṃ karotīti
children.translated_text: Since, when <s>prāṇa</s> is present, the instruments obtain their own being, <s>prāṇa</s> too, like a bird in a cage, causes the movement of everything.
It is called <s>prāṇa</s> because it breathes.

children.text: tathāpanayanād apānas tatra yat spandanaṃ tad api sāmānyavṛttir indriyasya
children.translated_text: Likewise, because it carries away, it is <s>apāna</s>; the pulsation there is also the common activity of the faculty.

children.text: tathā samāno madhyadeśavartī ya āhārādīnāṃ samaṃ nayanāt samāno vāyus tatra yat spandanaṃ tat sāmānyakaraṇavṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise <s>samāna</s>, located in the middle region, is the wind called <s>samāna</s> because it conducts food and the like evenly; the pulsation there is the common activity of the instruments.

children.text: tathordhvārohaṇād utkarṣād unnayanād vodāno nābhideśamastakāntargocaras tatrodāne yat spandanaṃ tat sarvendriyāṇāṃ sāmānyā vṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise, because of rising upward, elevation, or leading upward, <s>udāna</s> has its sphere between the navel region and the head; the pulsation in that <s>udāna</s> is the common activity of all the faculties.

children.text: kiṃca śarīravyāptir ābhyantaravibhāgaśca yena kriyate 'sau śarīravyāptyākāśavad vyānaḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, that by which the pervasion of the body and its internal division are effected is <s>vyāna</s>, pervading the body like space.

children.text: tatra yat spandanaṃ tat karaṇajālasya sāmānyā vṛttir iti
children.translated_text: The pulsation there is the common activity of the network of instruments.

children.text: evam ete pañca vāyavaḥ sāmānyakaraṇavṛttiriti vyākhyātās trayodaśavidhasyāpi karaṇasāmānyā vṛttir ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus these five winds have been explained as the common activity of the instruments; the meaning is that they are the common activity of the thirteenfold instrument as well.
The four operate simultaneously.
When buddhi, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and mind are connected with each individual faculty, there is a group of four.
In regard to a seen object, in the determination of each object, the activity of the four is simultaneous.

children.text: buddhyahaṃkāramanaścakṣūṃṣi yugapad ekakālaṃ rūpaṃ paśyanti sthāṇurayam iti
children.translated_text: Buddhi, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, mind, and the eyes see form simultaneously, at one time, as in 'this is a post.'
Buddhi, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, mind, and the tongue grasp taste simultaneously.
Buddhi, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, mind, and the nose grasp smell simultaneously.
So also the skin and the ear.
Moreover, its operation is also specified as sequential.
'Its' means that the activity of the four also occurs sequentially.

children.text: yathā kaścit pathi gacchan dūrād eva dṛṣṭvā sthāṇur ayaṃ puruṣo veti saṃśaye sati
children.translated_text: For example, someone walking on a road, having seen from afar, has a doubt: 'Is this a post or a man?'
Then he sees on it an attached sign, or a bird.

children.text: tatas tasya manasā saṃkalpite saṃśaye vyavacchedabhūtā buddhir bhavati sthāṇur ayam iti
children.translated_text: After that, when the doubt has been conceived by his mind, buddhi arises as the exclusion of that doubt: 'This is a post.'
Then <s>ahaṃkāra</s> too, for the purpose of certainty, says, 'It is certainly a post.'
Thus the sequential activity of buddhi, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, mind, and the eye is observed.
As with form, so it should also be understood with sound and the other objects.
With regard to what is seen, that is, in the sphere of visible objects.
And what else? Even so, with regard to the unseen, the activity of the three has that as its antecedent.

children.text: adṛṣṭe 'nāgate 'tīte ca kāle buddhyahaṃkāramanasāṃ rūpe cakṣuḥpūrvikā trayasya vṛttiḥ sparśe tvakpūrvikā gandhe ghrāṇapūrvikā rase rasanapūrvikā śabde śravaṇapūrvikā buddhyahaṃkāramanasām anāgate bhaviṣyati kāle 'tīte ca tatpūrvikā vṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: With regard to what is unseen, namely in future and past time, the activity of buddhi, ahaṃkāra, and mind has the eye as antecedent in the case of form, the skin as antecedent in the case of touch, the nose as antecedent in the case of smell, the tongue as antecedent in the case of taste, and hearing as antecedent in the case of sound; for buddhi, ahaṃkāra, and mind, in future time and in past time, activity has that as its antecedent.
In the present, it is simultaneous and also sequential.
Moreover:
'Each its own' is a distributive repetition.

children.text: buddhyahaṃkāramanāṃsi svāṃ svāṃ vṛttiṃ parasparākūtahetukām ākūtādarasaṃbhrama iti
children.translated_text: Buddhi, ahaṃkāra, and mind each undertake their own activity, caused by one another's intention; intention, regard, and agitation are meant.
Buddhi, ahaṃkāra, and the others proceed in order to accomplish the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>.
Buddhi, having known the intention of ahaṃkāra, undertakes its own proper object.

children.text: kimartham iti cet puruṣārtha eva hetuḥ
children.translated_text: If one asks, 'For what purpose?' the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s> alone is the cause.

children.text: puruṣārthaḥ kartavya ityevam arthaṃ guṇānāṃ pravṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: The activity of the guṇas has this meaning: the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s> must be accomplished.
Therefore these instruments reveal the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>.
If they are unconscious, how do they act by themselves?

children.text: na kenacit kāryate karaṇaṃ puruṣārtha evaikaḥ kārayatīti vākyārthaḥ
children.translated_text: The meaning of the sentence is: the instrument is not made to act by anyone; the single purpose of <s>puruṣa</s> itself makes it act.

children.text: na kenacid īśvarena puruṣena kāryate prabodhyate karaṇam
children.translated_text: The instrument, beginning with buddhi, is not made to act or awakened by any Lord or person.
Of how many kinds is that buddhi and the rest? This is stated:
The instrument, beginning with <s>mahat</s>, should be known as thirteenfold.

children.text: pañca buddhīndriyāṇi cakṣurādīni pañca karmendriyāṇi vāgādīnīti trayodaśavidhaṃ karaṇam
children.translated_text: The five cognitive faculties beginning with the eye, and the five faculties of action beginning with speech: thus the instrument is thirteenfold.
What does it do?
He states this:
It performs taking up, holding, and illumination.

children.text: tatrāharaṇaṃ dhāraṇaṃ ca karmendriyāṇi kurvanti prakāśaṃ buddhīndriyāṇi
children.translated_text: Among these, the faculties of action perform taking up and holding, while the cognitive faculties perform illumination.
Of how many kinds is its effect?
That is stated:
And its effect is tenfold.

children.text: tasya karaṇasya kāryaṃ kartavyaṃ daśadhā daśaprakāram
children.translated_text: The effect, the thing to be done, of that instrument is tenfold, of ten kinds.

children.text: śabdasparśarūparasagandhākhyaṃ vacanādānaviharaṇotsargānandākhyam etad daśavidhaṃ kāryaṃ buddhīndriyaiḥ prakāśitaṃ karmendriyāṇyāharanti dhārayanti ceti
children.translated_text: That which is called sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, and that which is called speech, grasping, moving about, excretion, and pleasure: this tenfold effect, illuminated by the cognitive faculties, is taken up and held by the faculties of action.
Moreover:
The internal organ means buddhi, ahaṃkāra, and mind; it is threefold because of the distinctions beginning with <s>mahat</s>.
And the external is tenfold.

children.text: buddhīndriyāṇi pañca karmendriyāṇi pañca daśavidham etat karaṇaṃ bāhyam
children.translated_text: The five cognitive faculties and the five faculties of action: this tenfold instrument is external.
That is called the object of the three, the enjoyable field of buddhi, ahaṃkāra, and mind.

children.text: sāṃpratakālaṃ śrotraṃ vartamānam eva śabdaṃ śṛṇoti nātītaṃ na ca bhaviṣyantaṃ cakṣurapi vartamānaṃ rūpaṃ paśyati nātītaṃ nānāgataṃ tvag vartamānaṃ sparśaṃ jihvā vartamānaṃ rasaṃ nāsikā vartamānaṃ gandhaṃ nātītānāgataṃ ceti
children.translated_text: In present time, hearing hears only a present sound, not a past or future one; the eye too sees a present form, not a past or future one; the skin experiences present touch, the tongue present taste, and the nose present smell, not past or future smell.

children.text: evaṃ karmendriyāṇi vāg vartamānaṃ śabdam uccārayati nātītaṃ nānāgataṃ ca
children.translated_text: In the same way among the faculties of action, speech utters a present sound, not a past or future one.

children.text: pāṇī vartamānaṃ ghaṭam ādadāte nātītam anāgataṃ ca
children.translated_text: The two hands take up a present pot, not one that is past or future.

children.text: pādau vartamānaṃ panthānaṃ viharato nātītaṃ nāpyanāgatam
children.translated_text: The two feet move along a present path, not a past or future one.

children.text: pāyūpasthau ca vartamānāvutsargānandau kuruto nātītau nānāgatau
children.translated_text: The anus and generative organ, being present, perform excretion and pleasure, not past or future ones.
Thus the external instrument has been described as belonging to present time.
The internal instrument belongs to the three times.

children.text: buddhyahaṃkāramanāṃsi trikālaviṣayāṇi buddhir vartamānaṃ ghaṭaṃ budhyate 'tītam anāgataṃ ceti
children.translated_text: Buddhi, ahaṃkāra, and mind have objects in the three times: buddhi cognizes a present pot, and also a past and future one.
Ahaṃkāra forms self-reference in the present, and also with regard to the past and future.

children.text: tathā mano vartamāne saṃkalpaṃ kurute 'tīte 'nāgate ca
children.translated_text: Likewise mind forms an intention in the present, and also in the past and future.
Thus the internal instrument belongs to the three times.

children.text: idānīm indriyāṇi kati saviśeṣaṃ viṣayaṃ gṛhṇanti kāni nirviśeṣam iti tad ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Now it is stated how many faculties apprehend an object with specification, and which apprehend one without specification.
Those cognitive faculties apprehend an object with specification.

children.text: saviśeṣaviṣayaṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ śabdasparśarūparasagandhān sukhaduḥkhamohayuktān buddhīndriyāṇi prakāśayanti
children.translated_text: The cognitive faculties illuminate for human beings sounds, touches, forms, tastes, and smells joined with pleasure, pain, and delusion, as objects with specification.
For gods, they illuminate objects without specification.

children.text: tathā karmendriyāṇāṃ madhye vāg bhavati śabdaviṣayā
children.translated_text: Likewise, among the faculties of action, speech has sound as its object.

children.text: devānāṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ ca vāg vadati ślokādīn uccārayati
children.translated_text: The speech of gods and human beings speaks and utters verses and the like.

children.text: tasmād devānāṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ ca vāgindriyaṃ tulyam
children.translated_text: Therefore the faculty of speech is the same for gods and human beings.
The remaining ones apart from speech, called hands, feet, anus, and generative organ, have the five objects.

children.text: pañca viṣayāḥ śabdādayo yeṣāṃ tāni pañcaviṣayāṇi
children.translated_text: Those whose objects are the five, beginning with sound, are five-object faculties.
Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell are present in the hand.
The foot moves about on the earth, which is characterized by the five, sound and the rest.
The anal faculty performs excretion, formed from the five.
Likewise the generative faculty delights semen, which has the five characteristics.
Buddhi is accompanied by the internal organ.
That means it is accompanied by ahaṃkāra and mind.
Because it enters into and apprehends every object.
It apprehends sound and the rest in all three times.

children.text: tasmāt trividhaṃ karaṇaṃ dvāri dvārāṇi śeṣāṇi karaṇānīti vākyaśeṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore the threefold instrument is the doorkeeper; the remaining instruments are the doors. This is the completion of the sentence.
And what else?
Those instruments that have been stated are specific forms of the guṇas.
Of what kind?
They are like lamps, illuminators of objects like a lamp.
They are mutually distinct.
That means dissimilar, having different objects.
That means having the guṇas as their object.
They are specific forms of the guṇas.
They are born from the guṇas.
The whole purpose belongs to <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: buddhīndriyāṇi karmendriyāṇyahaṃkāro manaścaitāni svaṃ svam arthaṃ puruṣasya prakāśya buddhau prayacchanti buddhisthaṃ kurvantītyarthaḥ
children.translated_text: The cognitive faculties, the faculties of action, ahaṃkāra, and mind disclose each of their own objects for <s>puruṣa</s> and hand them over to buddhi; that is, they make them present in buddhi.

children.text: yato buddhisthaṃ sarvaṃ viṣayasukhādikaṃ puruṣa upalabhyate
children.translated_text: For <s>puruṣa</s> experiences everything, such as pleasure from objects, as present in buddhi.
And here is another point.
Everything that has entered all the faculties, in all three times,
for each particular enjoyment, that is, with regard to enjoyment,

children.text: devamanuṣyatiryagbuddhīndriyakarmendriyadvāreṇa sāntaḥkaraṇā buddhiḥ sādhayati sampādayati yasmāt tasmāt saiva ca viśinaṣṭi pradhānapuruṣayor viṣayavibhāgaṃ karoti pradhānapuruṣāntaraṃ nānātvam ityarthaḥ
children.translated_text: buddhi, together with the inner organ, accomplishes and brings about through the channels of the cognitive and active faculties of gods, humans, and animals; therefore it alone also distinguishes, that is, makes the division of objects between <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>, meaning the difference and plurality between <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>.
'Subtle' means unattainable by those who have not undertaken the required austerities.

children.text: iyaṃ prakṛtiḥ sattvarajastamasāṃ sāmyāvastheyaṃ buddhir ayam ahaṃkāra etāni pañca tanmātrāṇyekādaśendriyāṇi pañca mahābhūtānyayam anyaḥ puruṣa ebhyo vyatiriktaḥ
children.translated_text: This is prakṛti, the state of equilibrium of sattva, rajas, and tamas; this is buddhi; this is ahaṃkāra; these are the five subtle elements, the eleven faculties, and the five great elements; and this other one, <s>puruṣa</s>, is distinct from them.

children.text: ityevaṃ bodhayati buddhir yasyāvāyād apavargo bhavati
children.translated_text: In this way buddhi teaches; from its determination liberation arises.
It was previously said that the objects are particular and non-particular.
Which objects are those? He shows them.

children.text: yāni pañca tanmātrāṇyahaṃkārād utpadyante tāni śabdatanmātraṃ sparśatanmātraṃ rūpatanmātraṃ rasatanmātraṃ gandhatanmātram
children.translated_text: The five subtle elements that arise from ahaṃkāra are the subtle element of sound, the subtle element of touch, the subtle element of form, the subtle element of taste, and the subtle element of smell.
These are called non-particulars.
For the gods these objects have the character of pleasure and are free from pain and delusion.

children.text: tebhyaḥ pañcabhyaḥ tanmātrebhyaḥ pañca mahābhūtāni pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśasaṃjñāni yānyutpadyante
children.translated_text: From those five subtle elements arise the five great elements, known as earth, water, fire, air, and ether.
These are remembered as particulars.

children.text: gandhatanmātrāt pṛthivī rūpatanmātrāt tejo rasatanmātrād āpaḥ sparśatanmātrād vāyuḥ śabdatanmātrād ākāśam iti
children.translated_text: From the subtle element of smell comes earth; from the subtle element of form, fire; from the subtle element of taste, water; from the subtle element of touch, air; and from the subtle element of sound, ether.
Thus these great elements have arisen.

children.text: ete viśeṣā mānuṣāṇāṃ viṣayāḥ śāntāḥ sukhalakṣaṇā ghorā duḥkhalakṣaṇā mūḍhā mohalakṣaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: These particulars are the objects of human beings: peaceful, having the character of pleasure; terrible, having the character of pain; and dull, having the character of delusion.

children.text: yathākāśaṃ kasyacid anavakāśād antargṛhāder nirgatasya sukhātmakaṃ śāntaṃ bhavati tad eva śītoṣṇavātavarṣābhibhūtasya duḥkhātmakaṃ ghoraṃ bhavati tad eva panthānaṃ gacchato vanamārgād bhraṣṭasya diṅmohān mūḍhaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: For example, space is peaceful and pleasant for someone who has come out from a confined place such as the inside of a house; that very same space becomes terrible and painful for one overwhelmed by cold, heat, wind, and rain; and that same space becomes dull through confusion about direction for one who is traveling on a road and has strayed from a forest path.

children.text: evaṃ vāyur gharmāt tasya śānto bhavati śītārtasya ghoro dhūlīśarkarāvimiśro 'tivān mūḍha iti
children.translated_text: So too air is peaceful for one suffering from heat, terrible for one afflicted by cold, and dull when it is excessively windy and mixed with dust and gravel.
The same should be understood with regard to fire and the rest.
Now, there are other particulars.

children.text: sūkṣmāstanmātrāṇi yat saṃgṛhītaṃ sūkṣmaśarīraṃ mahadādiliṅgaṃ sadā tiṣṭhati saṃsarati ca te sūkṣmāḥ
children.translated_text: The subtle ones are the subtle elements: that subtle body, composed of the liṅga beginning with mahat, which has been gathered together, always remains and transmigrates; these are subtle.
Likewise, those born of mother and father are the increasers of the gross body.
At the season for conception, when mother and father unite, the mingled blood and semen within the womb cause the subtle body to grow.

children.text: tat sūkṣmaśarīraṃ punar mātur aśitapītanānāvidharasena nābhīnibandhenāpyāyate
children.translated_text: That subtle body is then nourished through its connection with the navel by the various kinds of sap from what the mother has eaten and drunk.

children.text: tathā prārabdhaṃ śarīraṃ sūkṣmair mātāpitṛjaiśca saha mahābhūtaistridhā viśeṣaiḥ pṛṣṭhodarajaṅghākaṭyuraḥśiraḥprabhṛti ṣaṭkauśikaṃ pañcabhautikaṃ rudhiramāṃsasnāyuśukrāsthimajjāsaṃbhṛtam
children.translated_text: In this way the body that has begun, together with the subtle elements born of mother and father and with the great elements as threefold particulars, becomes six-sheathed, made of the five elements, complete with back, belly, thighs, hips, chest, head, and the rest, and filled with blood, flesh, sinew, semen, bone, and marrow.

children.text: ākāśo 'vakāśadānād vāyur vardhanāt tejaḥ pākād āpaḥ saṃgrahāt pṛthivī dhāraṇāt
children.translated_text: Ether functions by giving space, air by growth, fire by digestion, water by cohesion, and earth by support.
Endowed with all its limbs, it comes forth from the mother's womb.
Thus these particulars are of three kinds.
Here someone asks:
Which are permanent, and which are impermanent?
The subtle ones among them are fixed.

children.text: sūkṣmās tanmātrasaṃjñakās teṣāṃ madhye niyatā nityāḥ
children.translated_text: The subtle ones, called subtle elements, are fixed among them, that is, permanent.

children.text: tair ārabdhaṃ śarīraṃ karmavaśāt paśumṛgapakṣisarīsṛpasthāvarajātiṣu saṃsarati dharmavaśād indrādilokeṣu
children.translated_text: The body begun by them transmigrates, according to the force of karma, among the species of domestic animals, wild animals, birds, reptiles, and plants, and, according to the force of dharma, in the worlds beginning with that of Indra.

children.text: evam etanniyataṃ sūkṣmaśarīraṃ saṃsarati na yāvajjñānam utpadyate
children.translated_text: Thus this fixed subtle body transmigrates until knowledge arises.

children.text: utpanne jñāne vidvāñcharīraṃ tyaktvā mokṣaṃ gacchati
children.translated_text: When knowledge has arisen, the wise person, having abandoned the body, goes to liberation.

children.text: tasmād ete viśeṣāḥ sūkṣmā nityā iti
children.translated_text: Therefore these subtle particulars are permanent.
Those born of mother and father cease.

children.text: tat sūkṣmaśarīraṃ parityajehaiva prāṇatyāgavelāyāṃ mātāpitṛjā nivartante
children.translated_text: When that subtle body is abandoned here at the very time of giving up the vital breath, the elements born of mother and father cease.

children.text: maraṇakāle mātāpitṛjaṃ śarīram ihaiva nivṛttya bhūmyādiṣu pralīyate yathātattvam
children.translated_text: At the time of death, the body born of mother and father ceases here and dissolves into earth and the other elements, each according to its true principle.

children.text: sūkṣmaṃ ca kathaṃ saṃsarati tad āha ||
children.translated_text: And how does the subtle body transmigrate? He states this.

children.text: yadā lokā anutpannāḥ pradhānādisarge tadā sūkṣmaśarīram utpannam iti
children.translated_text: When the worlds had not yet arisen, at the creation beginning with <s>pradhāna</s>, then the subtle body was produced.
What else? It is unattached.
It is not joined to the places of animals, gods, or humans.
Because of its subtlety, it is unattached anywhere.
It transmigrates, moving with unobstructed passage through mountains and the like.
It is fixed, that is, permanent.
So long as knowledge does not arise, it transmigrates.

children.text: tacca mahadādisūkṣmaparyantaṃ mahān ādau yasya tanmahadādi buddhir ahaṃkāro mana iti pañca tanmātrāṇi
children.translated_text: And that, extending from mahat down to the subtle, is called 'beginning with mahat': mahat is first in it; it consists of buddhi, ahaṃkāra, mind, and the five subtle elements.

children.text: sūkṣmaparyantaṃ tanmātraparyantaṃ saṃsarati śūlagrahapipīlikāvat trīn api lokān
children.translated_text: Extending to the subtle means extending to the subtle elements; it transmigrates through all three worlds like a spear-bearing graha or an ant.
It is without enjoyment, devoid of experience.

children.text: tat sūkṣmaśarīraṃ pitṛmātṛjena bāhyenopacayena kriyādharmagrahaṇād bhogeṣu samarthaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ
children.translated_text: The meaning is that this subtle body becomes capable of experiences through external increase born of father and mother and through the acquisition of action and dharma.
It is perfumed by dispositions.

children.text: purastād bhāvān dharmādīn vakṣyāmas tair adhivāsitam uparañjitam
children.translated_text: Earlier we shall explain the dispositions beginning with <s>dharma</s>; by them the subtle mark is perfumed, that is, colored.
This is the <s>liṅga</s>.
At the time of dissolution, the subtle body, extending from <s>mahat</s> down to the subtle elements and furnished with the faculties, dissolves into <s>pradhāna</s>.

children.text: asaṃsaraṇayuktaṃ sad ā sargakālam atra vartate
children.translated_text: Being without connection with transmigration, it remains here until the time of creation.
Being bound by the bond of delusion about <s>prakṛti</s>, it is incapable of actions such as transmigration.
Again, at the time of creation it transmigrates; therefore the <s>liṅga</s> is subtle.

children.text: kiṃprayojanena trayodaśavidhaṃ karaṇaṃ saṃsaratītyevaṃ codite satyāha ||
children.translated_text: When the question is raised, 'For what purpose does the thirteenfold faculty transmigrate?', he says this:

children.text: citraṃ yathā kuḍyāśrayam ṛte na tiṣṭhati sthāṇvādibhyaḥ kīlakādibhyo vinā chāyā na tiṣṭhati tair vinā na bhavati
children.translated_text: Just as a painting does not remain without the support of a wall, and a shadow does not remain without posts and the like, pegs and the like, and does not exist without them,

children.text: ādigrahaṇād yathā śaityaṃ vinā nāpo bhavanti śaityaṃ vādbhir vināgnir uṣṇaṃ vinā vāyuḥ sparśaṃ vinākāśam avakāśaṃ vinā pṛthivī gandhaṃ vinā tadvat
children.translated_text: and, by taking the word 'and so on,' just as waters do not exist without coldness, nor coldness without waters, nor fire without heat, nor wind without touch, nor space without room, nor earth without smell, so too,

children.text: etena dṛṣṭāntena nyāyena vināviśeṣair aviśeṣaistanmātrair vinā na tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: by this example and reasoning, without particular entities, the non-particulars, the subtle elements, do not remain.
Now the particular elements are stated: the body consists of the five elements.

children.text: vaiśeṣiṇā śarīreṇa vinā kva liṅgasthānaṃ ceti
children.translated_text: Without a particularized body, where would there be a place for the <s>liṅga</s>?
It would be without support.
That means that the <s>liṅga</s>, the thirteenfold faculty, would be without a support.
For what purpose is that stated?
<s>Pradhāna</s> acts because the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s> is to be accomplished.
And that purpose is twofold: it has the form of apprehension of sound and the other objects, and it has the form of apprehension of the difference between the guṇas and <s>puruṣa</s>.
The apprehension of sound and the other objects is the attainment of experiences such as smell in the worlds beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>.
The apprehension of the difference between the guṇas and <s>puruṣa</s> is liberation.

children.text: tasmād uktaṃ puruṣārthahetukam idaṃ sūkṣmaśarīraṃ pravartata iti
children.translated_text: Therefore it was said that this subtle body acts because its cause is the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>.
In connection with cause and effect, the cause is <s>dharma</s> and the rest.
The effect, such as upward movement, we shall explain just below.
'In connection' means by association.
Because <s>prakṛti</s>, that is <s>pradhāna</s>, possesses all-pervasiveness,

children.text: yathā rājā svarāṣṭre vibhutvād yad yad icchati tat tat karotīti tathā prakṛteḥ sarvatra vibhutvayogānnimittanaimittikaprasaṅgena vyavatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: just as a king, because of his sovereignty in his own realm, does whatever he wishes, so, because <s>prakṛti</s> is all-pervasive everywhere, it establishes arrangement through the connection of cause and effect.

children.text: pṛthak pṛthag dehadhāraṇe liṅgasya vyavasthāṃ karoti
children.translated_text: It makes the arrangement of the <s>liṅga</s> for the assumption of separate bodies, one after another.

children.text: liṅgaṃ sūkṣmaiḥ paramāṇubhistanmātrairupacitaṃ śarīraṃ trayodaśavidhakaraṇopetaṃ mānuṣadevatiryagyoniṣu vyavatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: The <s>liṅga</s>, a body accumulated from subtle atoms, the subtle elements, and furnished with the thirteenfold faculty, becomes established in human, divine, and animal wombs.
How?
Like an actor.

children.text: yathā naṭaḥ paṭāntareṇa praviśya devo bhūtvā nirgacchati punar mānuṣaḥ punar vidūṣaka evaṃ liṅgaṃ nimittanaimittikaprasaṅgenodarāntaḥ praviśya hastī strī pumān bhavati
children.translated_text: Just as an actor enters with a different costume and comes out as a god, then again as a human being, then again as a clown, so the <s>liṅga</s>, through the connection of cause and effect, enters inside the womb and becomes an elephant, a woman, or a man.
It has been said that the <s>liṅga</s>, perfumed by dispositions, transmigrates.
What, then, are those dispositions? He says:
The dispositions are considered to be of three kinds: innate, natural, and derivative.
Among these, the innate are as follows.

children.text: bhagavataḥ kapilasyādisarga utpadyamānasya catvāro bhāvāḥ sahotpannā dharmo jñānaṃ vairāgyam aiśvaryam iti
children.translated_text: For the blessed <s>Kapila</s>, when he was born at the first creation, four dispositions were born together with him: <s>dharma</s>, knowledge, dispassion, and sovereignty.
The natural ones are described.
<s>Brahmā</s> had four sons: <s>Sanaka</s>, <s>Sanandana</s>, <s>Sanātana</s>, and <s>Sanatkumāra</s>.

children.text: teṣām utpannakāryakāraṇānāṃ śarīriṇāṃ ṣoḍaśavarṣāṇām ete bhāvāścatvāraḥ samutpannāstasmād ete prakṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: When they had bodies, with cause and effect already arisen, and were sixteen years old, these four dispositions arose in them; therefore these are natural.

children.text: tathā vaikṛtā yathācāryamūrtiṃ nimittaṃ kṛtvāsmadādīnāṃ jñānam utpadyate
children.translated_text: Likewise the derivative are as follows: for people such as ourselves, knowledge arises by taking the form of a teacher as the cause.

children.text: jñānād vairāgyaṃ vairāgyād dharmo dharmād aiśvaryam iti
children.translated_text: From knowledge comes dispassion, from dispassion <s>dharma</s>, and from <s>dharma</s> sovereignty.

children.text: ācāryamūrtirapi vikṛtir iti tasmād vaikṛtā ete bhāvā ucyante yair adhivāsitaṃ liṅgaṃ saṃsarati
children.translated_text: The form of the teacher too is a modification; therefore these dispositions are called derivative, and by them the <s>liṅga</s>, being perfumed, transmigrates.
These four dispositions are sāttvika.
The tāmasa dispositions are their opposites.

children.text: sāttvikam etad rūpaṃ tāmasam asmād viparyastam ityatra vyākhyātāḥ
children.translated_text: They have been explained in the statement, 'This form is sāttvika; the tāmasa is the reverse of this.'

children.text: evam aṣṭau dharmo jñānaṃ vairāgyam aiśvaryam adharmo 'jñānam avairāgyam anaiśvaryam iti
children.translated_text: Thus there are eight: <s>dharma</s>, knowledge, dispassion, sovereignty, non-dharma, ignorance, non-dispassion, and lack of sovereignty.

children.text: aṣṭau bhāvāḥ kva vartante dṛṣṭāḥ karaṇāśrayiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Where are the eight dispositions observed to occur? They depend on the faculty.
Buddhi is the faculty; they depend on it.

children.text: etad uktam adhyavasāyo buddhir dharmo jñānam iti
children.translated_text: This has been stated in the words, 'Determination is buddhi: <s>dharma</s>, knowledge,' and so on.

children.text: kāryaṃ dehas tadāśrayāḥ kalalādyā ye mātṛjā ityuktāḥ
children.translated_text: The effect is the body; those that depend on it have been stated as the maternal products beginning with the embryo-fluid.

children.text: śukraśoṇitasaṃyoge vivṛddhihetukāḥ kalalādyā budbudamāṃsapeśīprabhṛtayastathā kaumārayauvanasthaviratvādayo bhāvā annapānarasanimittā niṣpadyante
children.translated_text: When semen and blood unite, the forms beginning with embryo-fluid, such as bubble and lump of flesh, arise as causes of growth; likewise the conditions of childhood, youth, old age, and so on are produced because of the essence of food and drink.
Therefore they are said to depend on the effect; they arise because of the enjoyment of objects such as food.
What was stated as 'through the connection of cause and effect' is explained here:
By <s>dharma</s> there is upward going.
Taking <s>dharma</s> as the cause, it goes upward.

children.text: ūrdhvam ityaṣṭau sthānāni gṛhyante tad yathā brāhmaṃ prājāpatyaṃ saumyam aindraṃ gāndharvaṃ yākṣaṃ rākṣasaṃ paiśācam iti
children.translated_text: By 'upward' eight stations are understood, namely: <s>Brāhma</s>, <s>Prājāpatya</s>, <s>Saumya</s>, <s>Aindra</s>, <s>Gāndharva</s>, <s>Yākṣa</s>, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, and <s>Paiśāca</s>.
The subtle body goes there.
Non-dharma is the cause for births among domestic animals, wild animals, birds, reptiles, and finally immovable beings.
And further, by knowledge there is release.
Release is knowledge of the twenty-five principles.
With that as the cause, there is release, liberation.
Then the subtle body ceases, and the supreme self is declared.
From the opposite, bondage is held to occur.
Ignorance is the cause.

children.text: sa caiva naimittikaḥ prākṛto vaikāriko dākṣiṇikaśca bandha iti vakṣyati purastāt
children.translated_text: And this bondage too, as will be stated later, is causal, natural, modified, and connected with sacrificial gifts.
This is what was said:

children.text: prākṛtena ca bandhena tathā vaikārikeṇa ca
children.translated_text: By natural bondage, and likewise by modified bondage,
and by the third, connected with sacrificial gifts, one is bound; one is not released by anything else.
So too there is another cause.

children.text: yathā kasyacid vairāgyam asti na tattvajñānaṃ tasmād ajñānapūrvād vairāgyāt prakṛtilayo mṛto 'ṣṭāsu prakṛtiṣu pradhānabuddhyahaṃkāratanmātreṣu līyate na mokṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For example, someone has dispassion but not knowledge of the principles; therefore, because his dispassion is preceded by ignorance, when he dies as one dissolved into <s>prakṛti</s>, he is dissolved into the eight <s>prakṛti</s>s, namely <s>pradhāna</s>, <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and the subtle elements; this is not liberation.
After that he transmigrates again.
So too there is this rajasic attachment.

children.text: yajāmi dakṣiṇāṃ dadāmi yenāmuṣmiṃlloke 'tra yad divyaṃ mānuṣaṃ sukham anubhavāmi ||
children.translated_text: 'I sacrifice, I give sacrificial gifts, so that in the other world I may experience there whatever divine and human happiness exists.'
From this rajasic attachment transmigration arises.
Likewise, from lordly power there is non-obstruction.
This <s>aiśvarya</s> (lordly power) is eightfold, endowed with aṇimā and the other powers.

children.text: tasmād aiśvaryanimittād avighāto naimittiko bhavati brāhmādiṣu sthāneṣvaiśvaryaṃ na vihanyate ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the cause consisting in <s>aiśvarya</s>, there is causal non-obstruction: in states beginning with that of <s>Brahmā</s>, lordly power is not obstructed.
Moreover, from the opposite there is reversal.
The reversal of that non-obstruction is obstruction.
Because of lack of <s>aiśvarya</s>, one is obstructed everywhere.

children.text: eṣa nimittaiḥ saha naimittikaḥ ṣoḍaśavidho vyākhyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This sixteenfold causal effect, together with its causes, has been explained.
Of what nature is it? He states this.

children.text: yathaiṣa ṣoḍaśavidho nimittanaimittikabhedo vyākhyāta eṣa pratyayasarga ucyate
children.translated_text: This sixteenfold distinction of cause and effect that has just been explained is called <s>pratyayasarga</s> (the creation of dispositions).

children.text: pratyayo buddhir ityukto 'dhyavasāyo buddhir dharmo jñānam ityādi
children.translated_text: <s>Pratyaya</s> has been said to be <s>buddhi</s>: determination is <s>buddhi</s>, and so are dharma, knowledge, and the rest.
And this <s>pratyayasarga</s> is divided fourfold, according to the distinctions called viparyaya, aśakti, tuṣṭi, and siddhi.
Among these, doubt and ignorance are viparyaya (error).

children.text: yathā kasyacit sthāṇudarśane sthāṇur ayaṃ puruṣo veti saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: For example, when someone sees a post, the doubt 'Is this a post or a man?' is uncertainty.
Aśakti is incapacity.

children.text: yathā tam eva sthāṇuṃ samyag dṛṣṭvā saṃśayaṃ chettuṃ na śaknotītyaśaktiḥ
children.translated_text: For example, when he has correctly seen that very post but is unable to cut off the doubt, that is incapacity.
Thus the third is called tuṣṭi (satisfaction).

children.text: yathā tam eva sthāṇuṃ jñātuṃ saṃśayituṃ vā necchati
children.translated_text: For example, when he does not wish either to know or to doubt that very post,
thinking, 'What is this to us?' that is satisfaction.
The fourth is called siddhi (accomplishment).

children.text: yathānanditendriyaḥ sthāṇum ārūḍhāṃ valliṃ paśyati śakuniṃ vā
children.translated_text: For example, when one whose senses are delighted sees a vine climbing on the post, or a bird,

children.text: tasya siddhir bhavati sthāṇur ayam iti
children.translated_text: then his accomplishment occurs: 'This is a post.'

children.text: evam asya caturvidhasya pratyayasargasya guṇavaiṣamyavimardena tasya bhedāstu pañcāśat
children.translated_text: In this way, through the mutual pressure of the inequality of the guṇas, this fourfold <s>pratyayasarga</s> has fifty subdivisions.

children.text: yo 'yaṃ sattvarajastamoguṇānāṃ vaiṣamyo vimardas tena tasya pratyayasargasya pañcāśadbhedā bhavanti
children.translated_text: That inequality and mutual pressure of the guṇas sattva, rajas, and tamas produces fifty subdivisions of that <s>pratyayasarga</s>.

children.text: tathā kvāpi sattvam utkaṭaṃ bhavati rajastamasī udāsīne kvāpi rajaḥ kvāpi tama iti
children.translated_text: Thus in one case sattva is predominant while rajas and tamas are neutral; in another, rajas is predominant; in another, tamas is predominant.
The subdivisions are now stated.
There are five subdivisions of viparyaya.

children.text: te yathā tamo moho mahāmohas tāmisro 'ndhatāmisra iti
children.translated_text: They are as follows: tamas, moha, mahāmoha, tāmisra, and andhatāmisra.
The variety among these subdivisions will be stated immediately afterward.
But incapacity has twenty-eight subdivisions, because of defects in the instruments.
These too we shall explain.

children.text: tathā ca tuṣṭir navadhordhvasrotasi rājasāni jñānāni
children.translated_text: Likewise tuṣṭi is ninefold; in the upward-flowing realm, the knowledges are rajasic.
Likewise siddhi is eightfold; in that same upward-flowing realm, the knowledges are sāttvic.
This will be stated in due order.
Now the subdivisions of viparyaya are stated.
First, tamas has an eightfold division.
Dissolution is divided because of ignorance.
One is dissolved into the eight <s>prakṛti</s>s: <s>pradhāna</s>, <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and the five subtle elements, making eight.

children.text: tatra līnam ātmānaṃ manyate mukto 'ham iti tamobheda eṣaḥ
children.translated_text: When, dissolved there, one thinks of oneself, 'I am liberated,' this is a subdivision of tamas.
The meaning is that the subdivision of eightfold moha is itself eightfold.

children.text: yatrāṣṭaguṇam aiśvaryaṃ tatra saṅgād indrādayo devā na mokṣaṃ prāpnuvanti
children.translated_text: Where there is eightfold <s>aiśvarya</s>, because of attachment to it gods such as <s>Indra</s> do not attain liberation.
And when that is exhausted, they transmigrate again; this is eightfold moha.
Mahāmoha is tenfold.

children.text: śabdasparśarūparasagandhā devānām ete pañca viṣayāḥ sukhalakṣaṇā mānuṣāṇām apyeta eva śabdādayaḥ pañca viṣayāḥ
children.translated_text: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell: these five objects, characterized by pleasure, belong to the gods; and for humans too these same five objects, beginning with sound, are present.
Thus, with respect to these ten, there is mahāmoha.
Tāmisra is eighteenfold.

children.text: aṣṭavidham aiśvaryaṃ dṛṣṭānuśravikā viṣayā daśaiteṣām aṣṭādaśānām
children.translated_text: The eightfold <s>aiśvarya</s> and the ten visible and scripturally heard objects make these eighteen.
They rejoice in the attainment of these eighteen and do not accept their loss; this eighteenfold imagining is tāmisra.

children.text: tathā tāmisram aṣṭaguṇaṃ aiśvaryaṃ dṛṣṭānuśravikā daśa viṣayāstathāndhatāmisro 'pyaṣṭādaśabheda eva
children.translated_text: Thus tāmisra concerns the eightfold <s>aiśvarya</s> and the ten visible and scripturally heard objects; and andhatāmisra too has eighteen subdivisions.

children.text: kiṃtu viṣayasaṃpattau saṃbhogakāle ya eva mriyate 'ṣṭaguṇaiśvaryād vā bhraśyate tatas tasya mahad duḥkham utpadyate
children.translated_text: But when, at the time of enjoyment upon attaining the objects, one dies, or falls from the eightfold <s>aiśvarya</s>, then great suffering arises for him.
That is andhatāmisra.

children.text: evaṃ viparyayabhedāstamaḥprabhṛtayaḥ pañca pratyekaṃ bhidyamānā dviṣaṣṭibhedāḥ saṃvṛttā iti
children.translated_text: Thus the subdivisions of viparyaya, beginning with tamas, are five, and when each is subdivided they amount to sixty-two subdivisions.
The subdivisions of incapacity are now stated.
It was stated that because of defects in the instruments there are twenty-eight subdivisions of incapacity.

children.text: tatraikādaśendriyavadhā bādhiryam andhatā prasuptir upajihvikā ghrāṇapāko mūkatā kuṇitvaṃ khāñjyaṃ gudāvartaḥ klaibyam unmāda iti
children.translated_text: Among these, the eleven injuries of the faculties are deafness, blindness, sleepiness, upajihvikā, impairment of smell, muteness, crookedness, lameness, gudāvarta, impotence, and madness.
Incapacity is stated together with the injuries of the intellect.
Together with those injuries of the intellect, incapacity has twenty-eight subdivisions.
There are seventeen injuries of the intellect.
But the seventeen impairments are due to the reverse of the divisions of satisfaction and the divisions of attainment.
The divisions of satisfaction are nine, and the divisions of attainment are eight.

children.text: ye te viparītaiḥ sahaikādaśa vadhā evam aṣṭāviṃśativikalpā aśaktir iti
children.translated_text: Those, together with their opposites, are the eleven impairments; thus incapacity has twenty-eight varieties.
From the point of view of reversal, the sequence of the divisions of satisfaction and attainment is to be understood.
Among these, satisfaction is said to be ninefold.
There are four internal satisfactions.
Those that arise in oneself are internal, and they are called <s>prakṛti</s>, acquisition, time, and fortune.
Among these, those called <s>prakṛti</s> are as follows.

children.text: yathā kaścit prakṛtiṃ vetti tasyāḥ saguṇatvanirguṇatvaṃ ca
children.translated_text: For example, someone knows <s>prakṛti</s> and its being with qualities and without qualities.

children.text: tena tattvaṃ tatkāryaṃ vijñāyaiva kevalaṃ tuṣṭastasya nāsti mokṣaḥ
children.translated_text: By that alone, having understood the principle and its effect, he is satisfied; for him there is no liberation.
This is the satisfaction called <s>prakṛti</s>.
That called acquisition is as follows.

children.text: yathā kaścid avijñāyaiva tattvānyupādānagrahaṇaṃ karoti tridaṇḍakamaṇḍaluvividikābhyo mokṣa iti tasyāpi nāsti mokṣa iti
children.translated_text: For example, someone, without truly understanding the principles, undertakes the taking up of requisites, thinking that liberation comes from the triple staff, water-pot, and mendicant's gear; for him too there is no liberation.
This is the satisfaction called acquisition.
Likewise, that called time is as follows.

children.text: kālena mokṣo bhaviṣyatīti kiṃ tattvābhyāsenetyeṣa kālākhyā tuṣṭiḥ
children.translated_text: 'Liberation will occur in time; what need is there for practice of the principles?' This is the satisfaction called time.
For him there is no liberation.
Likewise, that called fortune is as follows.
'Liberation will occur through fortune alone'; this is called fortune.
Thus satisfaction is fourfold.
The external ones are five, because of withdrawal from objects.
The external satisfactions arise from withdrawal from the five objects.
One withdraws from sound, touch, form, taste, and smell because one sees acquisition, protection, loss, attachment, and injury.

children.text: vṛddhinimittaṃ paśupālyavāṇijyapratigrahasevāḥ kāryā etad arjanaṃ duḥkham
children.translated_text: For the sake of increase, one must engage in cattle-keeping, trade, receiving gifts, and service; this acquisition is painful.
There is pain in protecting what has been acquired.
Because it is depleted by enjoyment, there is the pain of loss.

children.text: tathā viṣayopabhogasaṅge kṛte nāstīndriyāṇām upaśama iti saṅgadoṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise, when attachment to the enjoyment of objects has arisen, there is no calming of the senses; this is the fault of attachment.
Likewise, there is no enjoyment without harming beings; this is the fault of injury.
Thus, from seeing the faults beginning with acquisition, five satisfactions arise from withdrawal from the five objects.
In this way, by the distinction between internal and external, there are nine satisfactions.

children.text: tāsāṃ nāmāni śāstrāntare proktānyaṃbhaḥ salilam ogho vṛṣṭiḥ sutamaḥ pāraṃ sunetraṃ nārīkam anuttamāmbhasikam iti
children.translated_text: Their names are stated in another treatise as Ambhas, Salila, Ogha, Vṛṣṭi, Sutamas, Pāra, Sunetra, Nārīka, and Anuttamāmbhasika.

children.text: āsāṃ tuṣṭīnāṃ viparītā aśaktibhedād buddhivadhā bhavanti
children.translated_text: The opposites of these satisfactions, as divisions of incapacity, become impairments of buddhi.

children.text: tad yathānambho 'salilam anogha ityādivaiparītyād buddhivadhā iti
children.translated_text: For example, through the opposites such as non-Ambhas, non-Salila, non-Ogha, and so on, they are impairments of buddhi.
Attainment is now stated.
Reasoning.
For example, someone constantly reasons.

children.text: kim iha satyaṃ kiṃ paraṃ kiṃ naiḥśreyasaṃ kiṃ kṛtvā kṛtārthaḥ syām iti cintayato jñānam utpadyate
children.translated_text: As he thinks, 'What here is true? What is supreme? What is the highest good? By doing what would I become one who has accomplished his purpose?', knowledge arises.

children.text: pradhānād anya eva puruṣa ityanyā buddhir anyo 'haṃkāro 'nyāni tanmātrāṇīndriyāṇi pañca mahābhūtānīti
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s> is indeed other than <s>pradhāna</s>; buddhi is one thing, ahaṃkāra another, and the subtle elements, faculties, and five great elements are others.

children.text: evaṃ tattvajñānam utpadyate yena mokṣo bhavati
children.translated_text: In this way knowledge of the principles arises, through which liberation occurs.
This is the first attainment, called reasoning.

children.text: tathā śabdajñānāt pradhānapuruṣabuddhyahaṃkāratanmātrendriyapañcamahābhūtaviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ bhavati tato mokṣa iti
children.translated_text: Likewise, from knowledge gained through authoritative word there is knowledge concerning <s>pradhāna</s>, <s>puruṣa</s>, buddhi, ahaṃkāra, the subtle elements, the faculties, and the five great elements; from that comes liberation.
This is the attainment called word.

children.text: adhyayanād vedādiśāstrādhyayanāt pañcaviṃśatitattvajñānaṃ prāpya mokṣaṃ yāti
children.translated_text: Through study, that is, through study of the Veda and other treatises, one obtains knowledge of the twenty-five principles and goes to liberation.
This is the third attainment.
The threefold removal of suffering.
For the removal of the three kinds of suffering, internal, elemental, and divine, one approaches a teacher and then, through instruction, goes to liberation.
This is the fourth attainment.

children.text: eṣaiva duḥkhatrayabhedāt tridhā kalpanīyeti ṣaṭ siddhayaḥ
children.translated_text: This same one, because of the division of the three sufferings, is to be conceived as threefold; thus there are six attainments.
Likewise, obtaining a friend.

children.text: yathā kaścit suhṛjjñānam adhigamya mokṣaṃ gacchatyeṣā saptamī siddhiḥ
children.translated_text: For example, someone obtains knowledge from a friend and goes to liberation; this is the seventh attainment.
Giving.

children.text: yathā kaścid bhagavatāṃ pratyāśrayauṣadhitridaṇḍakuṇḍikādīnāṃ grāsācchādanādīnāṃ ca dānenopakṛtya tebhyo jñānam avāpya mokṣaṃ yāti
children.translated_text: For example, someone benefits venerable persons by giving lodging, medicine, triple staffs, water-pots, and the like, and also food, clothing, and the like; having obtained knowledge from them, he goes to liberation.
This is the eighth attainment.

children.text: āsām aṣṭānāṃ siddhīnāṃ śāstrāntare saṃjñāḥ kṛtāstāraṃ sutāraṃ tāratāraṃ pramodaṃ pramuditaṃ pramodamānaṃ ramyakaṃ sadāpramuditam iti
children.translated_text: For these eight attainments names have been made in another treatise: Tāra, Sutāra, Tāratāra, Pramoda, Pramudita, Pramodamāna, Ramyaka, and Sadāpramudita.

children.text: āsāṃ viparyayād buddher vadhā ye viparītāste 'śaktau nikṣiptāḥ
children.translated_text: From the reversal of these arise impairments of buddhi; those that are opposite have been placed under incapacity.
For example, one should understand non-Tāra, non-Sutāra, non-Tāratāra, and so on.
The divisions of incapacity have been stated to be twenty-eight.
These, together with the impairments of buddhi, are the eleven impairments of the faculties.

children.text: tatra tuṣṭiviparyayā nava siddhīnāṃ viparyayā aṣṭāvevam ete saptadaśabuddhivadhāḥ
children.translated_text: Among them, the reversals of the satisfactions are nine, and the reversals of the attainments are eight; thus these are the seventeen impairments of buddhi.

children.text: etaiḥ sahendriyavadhā aṣṭāviṃśatir aśaktibhedāḥ paścāt kathitā iti
children.translated_text: Together with these, the impairments of the faculties are the twenty-eight divisions of incapacity described later.
Thus the statement and explanation have been made only of error, incapacity, satisfaction, and attainment.
Moreover, before attainment there is a threefold goad.

children.text: siddheḥ pūrvā yā viparyayāśaktituṣṭayastā eva siddher aṅkuśas tadbhedād eva trividhaḥ
children.translated_text: The errors, incapacities, and satisfactions that precede attainment are themselves the goad of attainment; because of their divisions it is threefold.

children.text: yathā hastī gṛhītāṅkuśena vaśo bhavatyevaṃ viparyayāśaktituṣṭibhir gṛhīto loko 'jñānaṃ prāpnoti
children.translated_text: Just as an elephant becomes controlled by a grasped goad, so the world, grasped by error, incapacity, and satisfaction, reaches ignorance.
Therefore these are to be abandoned and attainment is to be cultivated.
From that attainment, knowledge of the principles arises; therefore liberation follows.

children.text: atha yad uktaṃ bhāvair adhivasitaṃ liṅgaṃ tatra bhāvā dharmādayo 'ṣṭāvuktā buddhipariṇāmā viparyayāśaktituṣṭisiddhipariṇatāḥ
children.translated_text: Now, regarding what was said, that the liṅga is perfumed by dispositions: there the dispositions, beginning with dharma, were stated to be eight transformations of buddhi, transformed into error, incapacity, satisfaction, and attainment.
That is the creation of experience called the disposition-creation.
And the <s>liṅga</s> and the creation of subtle elements extending as far as the fourteenfold class of beings have been stated.
Here one might ask: if the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s> is accomplished by just one kind of creation, what need is there for both kinds of creation?
Therefore he says:

children.text: bhāvaiḥ pratyayasargair vinā liṅgaṃ na tanmātrasargo na pūrvapūrvasaṃskārādṛṣṭakāritatvād uttarottaradehalambhasya
children.translated_text: Without the dispositions, that is, the creation of cognitive states, there is no <s>liṅga</s> and no creation of subtle elements, because the acquisition of each later body is caused by earlier and earlier impressions and unseen merit.

children.text: liṅgena tanmātrasargeṇa ca vinā bhāvanirvṛttirna sthūlasūkṣmadehasādhyatvād dharmādeḥ
children.translated_text: And without the <s>liṅga</s> and the creation of subtle elements, the accomplishment of dispositions does not occur, since <s>dharma</s> and the rest are to be effected by gross and subtle bodies.

children.text: anāditvācca sargasya bījāṅkuravad anyonyāśrayo na doṣāya tattajjātīyāpekṣitve 'pi tattadvyaktīnāṃ parasparānapekṣitvāt
children.translated_text: And because creation is beginningless, mutual dependence, as with seed and sprout, is not a fault; for even though each depends on something of its own class, the individual instances do not depend on one another.

children.text: tasmād bhāvākhyo liṅgākhyaśca dvividhaḥ pravartate sarga iti
children.translated_text: Therefore creation proceeds in two forms, called the creation of dispositions and the creation of the <s>liṅga</s>.
What else?

children.text: tatra daivam aṣṭaprakāraṃ brāhmaṃ prājāpatyaṃ saumyam aindraṃ gāndharvaṃ yākṣaṃ rākṣasaṃ paiśācam iti
children.translated_text: Among these, the divine is of eight kinds: <s>Brāhma</s>, <s>Prājāpatya</s>, <s>Saumya</s>, <s>Aindra</s>, <s>Gāndharva</s>, <s>Yākṣa</s>, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, and <s>Paiśāca</s>.
Domestic animals, wild animals, birds, reptiles, and immovable beings are the beings; thus the animal birth is fivefold.
The human womb is one alone.
Thus there are fourteen classes of beings.
In all three worlds the three <s>guṇas</s> exist.
Among them, where is which one predominant? This is stated:
'Above' means: in the eight divine stations there is an expanse of <s>sattva</s>, an extension of <s>sattva</s>.
Where <s>sattva</s> is strong, that is called upward <s>sattva</s>.
There too <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> are present.

children.text: tamoviśālo mūlataḥ paśvādiṣu sthāvarānteṣu sarvaḥ sargas tamasādhikyena vyāptaḥ
children.translated_text: From below, among animals and the rest down to immovable beings, the whole creation is an expanse of <s>tamas</s>, pervaded by a predominance of <s>tamas</s>.
There too <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s> are present.
In the middle, among human beings, <s>rajas</s> is strong.
There too <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s> are found.
Therefore human beings are mostly subject to suffering.
Thus 'from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a clump of grass' means from <s>Brahmā</s> down to immovable beings.

children.text: evam abhautikaḥ sargo liṅgasargo bhāvasargo bhūtasargo daivamānuṣatairyagyonā ityeṣa pradhānakṛtaḥ ṣoḍaśavidhaḥ sargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus this sixteenfold creation, produced by <s>pradhāna</s>, is non-elemental creation, the creation of the <s>liṅga</s>, the creation of dispositions, the creation of beings, and the divine, human, and animal wombs.

children.text: tatreti teṣu devamānuṣatiryagyoniṣu jarākṛtaṃ maraṇakṛtaṃ caiva duḥkhaṃ cetanaḥ caitanyavān puruṣaḥ prāpnoti na pradhānaṃ na buddhir nāhaṃkāro na tanmātrāṇīndriyāṇi mahābhūtāni ca
children.translated_text: Among those divine, human, and animal wombs, the conscious one, the sentient <s>puruṣa</s>, obtains suffering caused by old age and death; not <s>pradhāna</s>, not <s>buddhi</s>, not <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, nor the subtle elements, the senses, and the great elements.

children.text: kiyantaṃ kālaṃ puruṣo duḥkhaṃ prāpnotīti tad vivinakti
children.translated_text: For how long does <s>puruṣa</s> obtain suffering? He distinguishes this:
Until the cessation of the <s>liṅga</s>.

children.text: yat tan mahadādi liṅgaśarīreṇāviśya tatra vyaktībhavati tad yāvan na nivartate saṃsāraśarīram iti tāvat saṃkṣepeṇa triṣu sthāneṣu puruṣo jarāmaraṇakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpnoti
children.translated_text: That which, beginning with <s>mahat</s>, enters by means of the subtle body and becomes manifest there: so long as it does not cease as the body of transmigration, for that long, in brief, <s>puruṣa</s> obtains suffering caused by old age and death in the three stations.

children.text: liṅgasya ā vinivṛtter liṅgasya vinivṛttiṃ yāvat
children.translated_text: 'Until the cessation of the <s>liṅga</s>' means up to the cessation of the <s>liṅga</s>.

children.text: liṅganivṛttau mokṣo mokṣaprāptau nāsti duḥkham iti
children.translated_text: When the <s>liṅga</s> ceases, there is liberation; when liberation is attained, there is no suffering.
By what, then, does it cease?

children.text: yadā pañcaviṃśatitattvajñānaṃ syāt sattvapuruṣānyathākhyātilakṣaṇam idaṃ pradhānam iyaṃ buddhir ayam ahaṃkāra imāni pañca mahābhūtāni yebhyo 'nyaḥ puruṣo visadṛśa iti
children.translated_text: When knowledge of the twenty-five principles arises, characterized by the discernment that <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> are different: 'this is <s>pradhāna</s>, this is <s>buddhi</s>, this is <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, these are the five great elements, and <s>puruṣa</s> is other than them, unlike them.'
Thus from knowledge comes the cessation of the <s>liṅga</s>, and from that liberation.
What is the cause of <s>prakṛti</s>'s undertaking? This is stated:
The word 'iti' is used at the end and in indication.
In the act of <s>prakṛti</s>, in the operation of <s>prakṛti</s>, in the activity of <s>prakṛti</s>.

children.text: ya ārambho mahadādiviśeṣabhūtaparyantaḥ prakṛtermahān mahato 'haṃkāras tasmāt tanmātrāṇyekādaśendriyāṇi tanmātrebhyaḥ pañca mahābhūtānītyeṣaḥ
children.translated_text: The undertaking of <s>prakṛti</s> extends from <s>mahat</s> and the rest down to the specific gross beings: from <s>prakṛti</s> comes <s>mahat</s>, from <s>mahat</s> <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, from that the subtle elements and the eleven senses, and from the subtle elements the five great elements.
It is for the liberation of each <s>puruṣa</s>.
That is, with respect to each and every <s>puruṣa</s>.
The undertaking is for the liberation of those who have entered divine, human, and animal states.
How?
The undertaking, though seeming to be for itself, is for another.

children.text: yathā kaścit svārthaṃ tyaktvā mitrakāryāṇi karotyevaṃ pradhānam
children.translated_text: Just as someone, having abandoned his own interest, performs the affairs of a friend, so too does <s>pradhāna</s>.

children.text: puruṣo 'tra pradhānasya na kiṃcit pratyupakāraṃ karoti
children.translated_text: Here <s>puruṣa</s> does nothing in return for <s>pradhāna</s>.

children.text: svārtha iva na ca svārthaḥ parārtha eva
children.translated_text: It is as if for its own sake, yet it is not for its own sake; it is solely for another's sake.
The purpose is the apprehension of objects such as sound, and the apprehension of the difference between the guṇas and <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: triṣu lokeṣu śabdādiviṣayaiḥ puruṣā yojayitavyā ante mokṣeṇeti pradhānasya pravṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: The activity of <s>pradhāna</s> is this: <s>puruṣas</s> are to be joined with objects such as sound in the three worlds, and at the end with liberation.

children.text: tathā coktaṃ kumbhavat pradhānaṃ puruṣārthaṃ kṛtvā nivartata iti
children.translated_text: And it has been said likewise: like a potter, <s>pradhāna</s>, having accomplished the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>, ceases.
On this point it is said:
<s>Pradhāna</s> is unconscious, while <s>puruṣa</s> is conscious.

children.text: mayā triṣu lokeṣu śabdādibhir viṣayaiḥ puruṣo yojyo 'nte mokṣaḥ kartavya iti
children.translated_text: How can there be activity as if conscious, with the thought, 'I must join <s>puruṣa</s> in the three worlds with objects such as sound, and at the end liberation must be effected'?
How is there activity as if it were conscious?

children.text: satyaṃ kiṃtvacetānānām api pravṛttir dṛṣṭā nivṛttiśca
children.translated_text: True; but activity and cessation are observed even among unconscious things.
Because of this, he says:

children.text: yathā tṛṇādikaṃ gavā bhakṣitaṃ kṣīrabhāvena pariṇamya vatsavivṛddhiṃ karoti puṣṭe ca vatse nivartata evaṃ puruṣavimokṣanimittaṃ pradhānam iti
children.translated_text: Just as grass and the like, eaten by a cow, transform into the state of milk and cause the calf's growth, and when the calf is nourished, cease, so too <s>pradhāna</s> exists for the sake of <s>puruṣa</s>'s liberation.
This is the activity of what is insentient.
And further:

children.text: yathā loka iṣṭautsukye sati tasya nivṛttyarthaṃ kriyāsu pravartate gamanāgamanakriyāsu kṛtakāryo nivartate tathā puruṣasya vimokṣārthaṃ śabdādiviṣayopabhogalakṣaṇaṃ guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhilakṣaṇaṃ ca dvividham api puruṣārthaṃ kṛtvā pradhānaṃ nivartate
children.translated_text: Just as in the world, when there is eager desire for something, one engages in actions such as going and coming in order to end that desire, and, when the task has been done, ceases, so too <s>pradhāna</s>, having accomplished both forms of the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>--the enjoyment of objects such as sound and the apprehension of the difference between the guṇas and <s>puruṣa</s>--ceases.
What else?

children.text: yathā nartakī śṛṅgārādirasair itihāsādibhāvaiśca nibaddhagītavāditravṛttāni raṅgasya darśayitvā kṛtakāryā nṛtyānnivartate tathā prakṛtir api puruṣasyātmānaṃ prakāśya buddhyahaṃkāratanmātrendriyamahābhūtabhedena nivartate
children.translated_text: Just as a dancer, after showing the audience dances accompanied by song and music and structured by erotic and other sentiments and by narrative situations and the like, has accomplished her task and ceases from dancing, so too <s>prakṛti</s>, after revealing herself to <s>puruṣa</s> in the differentiated forms of buddhi, ahaṃkāra, the subtle elements, the senses, and the great elements, withdraws.
How, and what is the cause that makes her withdraw?
He states that:
By many kinds of means <s>prakṛti</s>, helpful to <s>puruṣa</s>, acts for the man who gives no help in return.
How?
By becoming divine, human, and animal; by having the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion; and by becoming objects such as sound.

children.text: evaṃ nānāvidhairupāyair ātmānaṃ prakāśyāham anyā tvam anya iti nivartate
children.translated_text: Having thus revealed herself by many kinds of means, saying, 'I am one thing and you are another,' she withdraws.

children.text: ato nityasya tasyārtham apārthaṃ carati kurute
children.translated_text: Therefore she acts for the sake of that eternal one, while it is for no sake of her own; she performs what has no purpose for herself.

children.text: yathā kaścit paropakārī sarvasyopakurute nātmanaḥ pratyupakāram īhata evaṃ prakṛtiḥ puruṣārthaṃ carati karotyapārthakam
children.translated_text: Just as some benefactor helps everyone and does not seek a return benefit for himself, so <s>prakṛti</s> acts for the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>, doing what is purposeless for herself.
It was said above that, after revealing herself, she withdraws.
And when she has withdrawn, what does she do? He states:

children.text: loke prakṛteḥ sukumārataraṃ na kiṃcid astītyevaṃ me matir bhavati
children.translated_text: In the world there is nothing more delicate than <s>prakṛti</s>: such is my thought.
By this the thought has arisen that she exists only for another's sake.
Why?

children.text: aham anena puruṣeṇa dṛṣṭāsmītyasya puṃsaḥ punardarśanaṃ nopaiti puruṣasyādarśanam upayātītyarthaḥ
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'I have been seen by this <s>puruṣa</s>,' she does not come again into sight for this man; the meaning is that she comes to be unseen by <s>puruṣa</s>.
There he describes what is more delicate.
Some say that <s>Īśvara</s> is the cause.
This ignorant creature is not master over his own pleasure and pain;

children.text: īśvaraprerito gacchet svargaṃ narakam eva vā ||
children.translated_text: driven by <s>Īśvara</s>, he goes either to heaven or to hell.
