Others, who hold inherent nature to be the cause, say:

children.text: kena śuddhīkṛtā haṃsā mayūrāḥ kena citritāḥ
children.translated_text: By whom were the swans made white? By whom were the peacocks made variegated?
By inherent nature alone, they say.
Here the Sāṃkhya teachers say:

children.text: nirguṇatvād īśvarasya kathaṃ saguṇāḥ prajā jāyeran
children.translated_text: Since <s>Īśvara</s> is without guṇas, how could creatures possessing guṇas be born from him?
Or how could they arise from <s>puruṣa</s>, which is likewise without guṇas?
Therefore it is reasonable that they arise from <s>prakṛti</s>.

children.text: yathā śuklebhyastantubhyaḥ śukla eva paṭo bhavati kṛṣṇebhyaḥ kṛṣṇa evetyevaṃ triguṇāt pradhānāt trayo lokāstriguṇāḥ samutpannā iti gamyate
children.translated_text: Just as from white threads there is only a white cloth, and from black threads only a black one, so it is understood that from the three-guṇa <s>pradhāna</s> the three worlds, consisting of the three guṇas, have arisen.

children.text: nirguṇa īśvaraḥ saguṇānāṃ lokānāṃ tasmādutpattir ayukteti
children.translated_text: Since <s>Īśvara</s> is without guṇas, the production from him of worlds possessing guṇas is therefore unreasonable.
By this <s>puruṣa</s> has also been explained.

children.text: tathā keṣāṃcit kālaḥ kāraṇam ityuktaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Likewise, for some, time is said to be the cause, as stated:

children.text: kālaḥ pacati bhūtāni kālaḥ saṃharate jagat
children.translated_text: Time cooks beings; time withdraws the world.

children.text: kālaḥ supteṣu jāgarti kālo hi duratikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Time keeps watch among those who sleep; for time is hard to overcome.
The manifest, the unmanifest, and <s>puruṣa</s> are the three realities; time is included within them.
For it is manifest.
Because time too has the function of doing all things, <s>pradhāna</s> alone is the cause.
Inherent nature too is dissolved into this very same thing.

children.text: tasmāt kālo na kāraṇaṃ nāpi svabhāva iti
children.translated_text: Therefore time is not the cause, nor is inherent nature.
Therefore <s>prakṛti</s> alone is the cause.
There is no other cause of <s>prakṛti</s>.

children.text: na punar darśanam upayāti puruṣasyātaḥ prakṛteḥ sukumārataraṃ subhogyataraṃ na kiṃcid īśvarādikāraṇam astīti me matir bhavati
children.translated_text: She does not come again into the sight of <s>puruṣa</s>; therefore I think there is no cause such as <s>Īśvara</s> more delicate or more fit to be enjoyed than <s>prakṛti</s>.

children.text: tathā ca loke rūḍhaṃ puruṣo muktaḥ puruṣaḥ saṃsaratīti ca
children.translated_text: And yet in the world it is conventionally established that '<s>puruṣa</s> is released' and '<s>puruṣa</s> transmigrates.'
When this is raised, he says:

children.text: tasmāt kāraṇāt puruṣo na badhyate nāpi mucyate nāpi saṃsarati yasmāt kāraṇāt prakṛtir eva nānāśrayā daivamānuṣatiryagyonyāśrayā buddhyahaṃkāratanmātrendriyabhūtasvarūpeṇa badhyate mucyate saṃsarati ceti
children.translated_text: For that reason <s>puruṣa</s> is not bound, nor is he released, nor does he transmigrate, because <s>prakṛti</s> alone, resting on many supports, resting in divine, human, and animal wombs, in the form of buddhi, ahaṃkāra, subtle elements, senses, and elements, is bound, released, and transmigrates.

children.text: atha mukta eva svabhāvāt sa sarvagataśca kathaṃ saṃsarati
children.translated_text: Now, if he is by nature released and all-pervading, how does he transmigrate?
Transmigration is for the sake of bringing about what has not yet been attained.

children.text: tena puruṣo badhyate puruṣo mucyate puruṣaḥ saṃsaratīti vyapadiśyate yena saṃsāritvaṃ na vidyate
children.translated_text: Therefore it is conventionally said, '<s>puruṣa</s> is bound,' '<s>puruṣa</s> is released,' and '<s>puruṣa</s> transmigrates,' though transmigratory status does not belong to him.
Through knowledge of the distinction between sattva and <s>puruṣa</s>, the true nature of <s>puruṣa</s> becomes manifest.

children.text: tadabhivyaktau kevalaḥ śuddho muktaḥ svarūpapratiṣṭhaḥ puruṣa iti
children.translated_text: When that is manifest, <s>puruṣa</s> is isolated, pure, released, and established in his own nature.

children.text: atra yadi puruṣasya bandho nāsti tato mokṣo 'pi nāsti
children.translated_text: Here, if there is no bondage of <s>puruṣa</s>, then there is no liberation either.
To this it is replied:

children.text: prakṛtir evātmānaṃ badhnāti mocayati ca yanna sūkṣmaśarīraṃ tanmātrakaṃ trividhakaraṇopetaṃ tat trividhena bandhena badhyate
children.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s> alone binds and releases herself. The subtle body, consisting of the subtle elements and furnished with the threefold instrument, is bound by the threefold bondage.
And it has been said:

children.text: prākṛtena ca bandhena tathā vaikārikeṇa ca
children.translated_text: By natural bondage, and likewise by derivative bondage,
and by the third, sacrificial bondage, one who is bound is released by no other.
That subtle body is joined with <s>dharma</s> and non-<s>dharma</s>.
And <s>prakṛti</s> is bound, <s>prakṛti</s> is released, and <s>prakṛti</s> transmigrates.
How is that?
It is stated:
By seven forms alone.

children.text: etāni sapta procyante dharmo jñānaṃ vairāgyam aiśvaryam adharmo 'jñānam avairāgyam anaiśvaryam
children.translated_text: These seven are taught: <s>dharma</s>, knowledge, dispassion, sovereignty, non-<s>dharma</s>, ignorance, non-dispassion, and lack of sovereignty.
These are the seven forms of <s>prakṛti</s>.

children.text: tair ātmānaṃ svaṃ badhnāti prakṛtir ātmānaṃ svenaiva
children.translated_text: By them <s>prakṛti</s> binds her own self, by herself alone.

children.text: saiva prakṛtiḥ puruṣasyārthaḥ puruṣārthaḥ kartavya iti vimocayatyātmānam ekarūpeṇa jñānena
children.translated_text: That very <s>prakṛti</s>, thinking, 'The purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>, the task for <s>puruṣa</s>, must be accomplished,' releases herself through one form, knowledge.
How does knowledge arise?

children.text: evam uktakrameṇa pañcaviṃśatitattvālocanābhyāsād iyaṃ prakṛtir ayaṃ puruṣa etāni pañcatanmātrendriyamahābhūtānīti puruṣasya jñānam utpadyate
children.translated_text: Through repeated examination, in the order already stated, of the twenty-five principles, knowledge arises for <s>puruṣa</s>: 'This is <s>prakṛti</s>; this is <s>puruṣa</s>; these are the five subtle elements, the senses, and the great elements.'

children.text: nāsmi nāham eva bhavāmi na me mama śarīraṃ tad yato 'ham anyaḥ śarīram anyat
children.translated_text: 'I am not this; I do not become this very thing; it is not mine; my body is not myself, since I am one thing and the body is another.'
"I am not": this is without remainder, free from <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle), without remainder.
Because it is not mistaken, it is pure.
Mistake is doubt; because it is free from mistake, it is free from doubt.

children.text: viśuddhaṃ kevalaṃ tad eva nānyad astīti mokṣakāraṇam
children.translated_text: That alone, pure and isolated, and nothing else, is the cause of liberation.
Knowledge arises, that is, becomes manifest: the knowledge of the twenty-five principles for <s>puruṣa</s>.
When there is knowledge, what does <s>puruṣa</s> do?

children.text: tena viśuddhena kevalajñānena puruṣaḥ prakṛtiṃ paśyati prekṣakavat prekṣakeṇa tulyam avasthitaḥ svasthaḥ
children.translated_text: By that pure and isolated knowledge, <s>puruṣa</s> sees <s>prakṛti</s>, like a spectator; he remains equal to a spectator, established in himself, self-abiding.
Just as a spectator at a theatre, standing apart, watches a dancer,
self-abiding means that he stands in himself; self-abiding means established in his own place.
What sort of <s>prakṛti</s> does he see?

One whose production has ceased, whose effects, <s>buddhi</s> and <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, have ceased, and which, because its purpose is fulfilled, has withdrawn from its seven forms, since the purposes of both have been brought to an end.

children.text: yaiḥ saptabhī rūpairdharmādibhir ātmānaṃ badhnāti tebhyaḥ saptabhyo rūpebhyo vinivṛttāṃ prakṛtiṃ paśyati ||
children.translated_text: He sees <s>prakṛti</s> withdrawn from those seven forms, beginning with <s>dharma</s>, by which it binds the self.

children.text: raṅgastha iti yathā raṅgastha ityevam upekṣaka ekaḥ kevalaḥ śuddhaḥ puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: "Standing on the stage": just as one stands on the stage, so the indifferent one, the single, isolated, pure <s>puruṣa</s>, stands apart.
Thinking, "I have been seen by him," <s>prakṛti</s> has stopped, has ceased.
One and the same <s>prakṛti</s> is the principal causal basis even of the three worlds.

children.text: na dvitīyā prakṛtir asti mūrtibhede jātibhedāt
children.translated_text: There is no second <s>prakṛti</s>, because difference of individual form entails difference of class.

children.text: evaṃ prakṛtipuruṣayor nivṛttāvapi vyāpakatvāt saṃyogo'sti na tu saṃyogakṛtaḥ sargaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, even when <s>prakṛti</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> have ceased from activity, there is conjunction because they are all-pervasive; but there is no creation produced by that conjunction.

children.text: sati saṃyoge 'pi tayoḥ prakṛtipuruṣayoḥ sargagatattvāt satyapi saṃyoge prayojanaṃ nāsti sargasya sṛṣṭeścaritārthatvāt
children.translated_text: Even though there is conjunction of those two, <s>prakṛti</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>, because creation has reached its end, there is no purpose in conjunction, since creation, the produced world, has accomplished its object.
<s>Prakṛti</s> has a twofold purpose: apprehension of objects such as sound, and apprehension of the difference between the guṇas and <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: ubhayatrāpi caritārthatvāt sargasya nāsti prayojanaṃ yaḥ punaḥsarga iti
children.translated_text: Since in both respects the purpose has been accomplished, there is no purpose for creation, that is, for further creation.

children.text: yathā dānagrahaṇanimitta uttamarṇādhamarṇayor dravyaviśuddhau satyapi saṃyoge na kaścid arthasaṃbandho bhavati
children.translated_text: Just as, when the debt has been cleared between creditor and debtor, whose relation was caused by giving and receiving, even if there is contact, there is no meaningful relation at all,
so too there is no purpose for <s>prakṛti</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: yadi puruṣasyotpanne jñāne mokṣo bhavati tato mama kasmānna bhavatīti
children.translated_text: If liberation comes for <s>puruṣa</s> when knowledge has arisen, then why does it not happen for me?
Therefore this is said:

children.text: yadyapi pañcaviṃśatitattvajñānaṃ samyagjñānaṃ bhavati tathāpi saṃskāravaśād dhṛtaśarīro yogī tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: Although knowledge of the twenty-five principles is right knowledge, nevertheless the yogin, holding a body because of saṃskāras (residual impressions), remains alive.
How?
Like the turning of a wheel, comparable to the spinning of a wheel.

children.text: yathā kulālaścakraṃ bhramayitvā ghaṭaṃ karoti mṛtpiṇḍaṃ cakram āropya
children.translated_text: Just as a potter, having set a wheel in motion, makes a pot after placing a lump of clay on the wheel,

children.text: punaḥ kṛtvā ghaṭaṃ paryāmuñcati cakraṃ bhramatyeva saṃskāravaśāt
children.translated_text: and, after making the pot, stops his work, yet the wheel itself continues to turn because of its residual momentum,
so, from the attainment of right knowledge, when right knowledge has arisen, <s>dharma</s> and the rest no longer arrive as causes.
These seven forms, which constitute bondage, have been burned by right knowledge.

children.text: yathā nāgninā dagdhāni bījāni prarohaṇasamarthānyevam etāni dharmādīni bandhanāni na samarthāni
children.translated_text: Just as seeds burned by fire are not capable of sprouting, so these bonds, <s>dharma</s> and the rest, are not capable.
When <s>dharma</s> and the rest no longer arrive as causes, one remains holding the body because of saṃskāras.
Why is there not, from knowledge, the destruction of present <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>?
Precisely because it is present, it too comes to destruction in the next moment.

children.text: jñānaṃ tvanāgatakarma dahati vartamānaśarīreṇa ca yat karoti tad apīti vihitānuṣṭhānakaraṇād iti
children.translated_text: But knowledge burns future karma, and also whatever one does with the present body, because one performs the prescribed observances.
When the saṃskāras are exhausted, at the fall of the body, there is liberation.
What is it characterized by?
This is said:

children.text: dharmādharmajanitasaṃskārakṣayāt prāpte śarīrabhede caritārthatvāt pradhānasya nivṛttāvaikāntikam avaśyam ātyantikam anantarhitaṃ kaivalyaṃ kevalabhāvānmokṣa ubhayam aikāntikātyantikam ityevaṃviśiṣṭaṃ kaivalyam āpnoti ||
children.translated_text: When the exhaustion of saṃskāras produced by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> has occurred, and when the separation from the body has been reached, because <s>pradhāna</s> has accomplished its purpose and has ceased, he attains <s>kaivalya</s>: absolute, necessarily so; ultimate, without interruption; liberation because it is the state of isolation. Thus both terms, absolute and ultimate, describe this <s>kaivalya</s>.
Liberation is the goal of <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: tadartham idaṃ guhyaṃ rahasyaṃ paramarṣiṇā śrīkapilarṣiṇā samākhyātaṃ samyag uktam
children.translated_text: For that purpose, this secret teaching, this mystery, was fully explained by the supreme seer, the venerable seer <s>Kapila</s>.

children.text: yatra jñāne bhūtānāṃ vaikārikāṇāṃ sthityutpattipralayā avasthānāvirbhāvatirobhāvāścintyante vicāryante
children.translated_text: In this knowledge, the continuance, origination, and dissolution of beings, which are evolutes, and their abiding, manifestation, and disappearance, are contemplated and examined.

children.text: yeṣāṃ vicārāt samyak pañcaviṃśatitattvavivecanātmikā sampadyate saṃvittir iti
children.translated_text: Through the examination of these, understanding is produced, consisting in the proper discrimination of the twenty-five principles.
The Sāṃkhya, taught by the sage <s>Kapila</s>, is indeed the cause of release from saṃsāra.

children.text: yatraitāḥ saptatir āryā bhāṣyaṃ cātra gauḍapādakṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Here are these seventy āryā verses, and here too is the commentary composed by <s>Gauḍapāda</s>.
These Sāṃkhyakārikās together with <s>Gauḍapāda</s>'s commentary are completed.
